collectedJobs.descriptionText:
We are looking for a Senior Forward Deployed Engineer to join the Customer Solutions team. You will be the technical authority embedded with our most complex customers, guiding them through deployment, architecture, onboarding, and the adoption of agentic development workflows. You bring deep hands-on experience from prior roles and use that depth to advise, design repeatable patterns, and drive customer outcomes end to end. You operate autonomously, own the technical success of your customers, and bring their experience back to shape how Coder builds and delivers.

This is not an execution-only role. You are equally comfortable doing deep technical work with a customer and stepping back to design the repeatable pattern behind it. You are energized by ambiguity, motivated by customer outcomes, and able to influence organizational change alongside the technical work.

 

What you'll do here 

 - Serve as the primary technical authority for post-sales customers, guiding deployment architecture, environment design, and adoption of Coder across both human and AI development workflows.

 - Own onboarding engagements end-to-end, ensuring customers move from contract to productive adoption with speed and confidence.

 - Lead engagements where architecture decisions, rollout patterns, or organizational dynamics are limiting customer health or growth.

 - Help customers implement the technical and organizational changes required to adopt agentic development practices at scale.

 - Design and document repeatable delivery patterns across onboarding, architecture, and adoption that can scale across customer segments.

 - Design and recommend reference architectures tailored to each customer's cloud environment, security posture, and organizational constraints.

 - Translate customer environment complexity into clear guidance on networking, ingress, identity, and infrastructure patterns.

 - Anticipate technical and operational risks, escalate to the right internal stakeholders, and track issues through to resolution.

 - Contribute to technical documentation, architecture guides, how-to resources, and statements of work that extend your impact across the customer base.

 - Capture structured product feedback from customer deployments and advocate directly with engineering and product teams for roadmap and usability improvements.

 

What we're looking for

 - 5+ years of experience in a Forward Deployed Engineering, Solutions Architect, Platform Engineering, or equivalent post-sales technical role, with a demonstrated track record of guiding enterprise customers through complex technical deployments.

 - Proven hands-on experience from a prior role designing and deploying cloud infrastructure on at least one major provider: AWS, Google Cloud, or Microsoft Azure; you have done the work and can speak to it with specificity.

 - 2+ years of production experience with Kubernetes: cluster design, workload scheduling, networking, storage, and operational lifecycle.

 - 2+ years of experience with Terraform or equivalent infrastructure-as-code tooling; you understand how enterprise teams structure, version, and maintain IaC at scale.

 - Solid understanding of Linux systems administration, including networking fundamentals: ingress controllers, proxies, load balancers, and DNS resolution in cloud-native environments.

 - Familiarity with CI/CD pipeline design and DevOps practices; you understand how code moves from commit to running workload in an enterprise context.

 - Working knowledge of cloud security and identity: IAM patterns, network segmentation, secrets management, and compliance-relevant controls.

 - Understanding of observability practices including logging, metrics, and tracing across distributed systems

 - Experience with AI tooling at both the user level (coding agents, assistants) and infrastructure level (model proxies, LLM routing layers such as LiteLLM).

 - Demonstrated ability to design repeatable delivery patterns, not just solve one-off problems.

 - Comfort working through organizational and workflow change alongside technical change with customers.

 - Strong verbal and written communication skills: you can hold a room with a senior infrastructure team and produce a clear architecture document without those being separate skills.

 - High customer empathy: you understand that the best technical solution does not always fit a customer's constraints, timeline, or organizational reality.

 - Self-directed, analytically minded, and comfortable operating with full autonomy in a startup environment.

 

Bonus tacos if you have 

 - (Tacos? If you need an ice-breaker, ask how we say thanks by giving tacos!)

 - Experience at both early-stage startups and larger software organizations.

 - Background as a Software Engineer, DevOps Engineer, or Platform Engineer before moving into a customer-facing role.

 - Familiarity with regulated environments: air-gapped deployments, network isolation, SOC 2, ISO 27001, GDPR, or DORA requirements.

 - Experience with disaster recovery design and multi-region availability patterns.

 - Cloud cost optimization experience, including rightsizing, reserved capacity, and FinOps practices.

 - Experience with Tailscale or similar overlay networking tools.

 - Kubernetes certification (CKA, CKAD, or CKS).

 - Open-source contributions.

 - Experience with Backstage.io or similar internal developer portals and platform tooling.

 - Prior work on or alongside a developer platform or platform engineering team.

 - Experience introducing new operating models or delivery patterns across post-sales or go-to-market teams.




ABOUT CODER

Coder is the leading platform for AI development Infrastructure, enabling enterprises to securely run human and AI-driven development workflows in consistent, governed environments. Coder provides self-hosted, agent-ready workspaces that unify developer productivity and platform governance. With Coder, enterprises can confidently evolve from human-only development to AI-assisted and autonomous workflows, without sacrificing security, compliance, or performance. Learn more at coder.com http://coder.com.




INTERVIEW PROCESS 

We believe that the interview process should be transparent, consistent, and enjoyable. We value your time and hope to complete the interview process in two to four weeks, if schedules allow.  Through your interviews, you will meet a mix of individual contributors, managers, and senior leaders. 




AI USE DURING THE INTERVIEW PROCESS

As an AI company, Coder embraces the use of AI tools, and we want to be transparent about our expectations as you navigate our interview process.  

Not permitted: Using AI assistance during conversational interviews.

Permitted: Using AI tooling for take-home assessments. Please flag where and to what extent it was used in your take-home. Your submission will not be penalized for using AI as long as it is done honestly.




OUR USE OF AI IN HIRING

We use AI tools to help manage our recruitment process efficiently and fairly. Specifically:

 - Ashby and Brainerr help us review inbound applications by surfacing candidates who best match the role requirements we've defined. This tool does not make hiring decisions; it helps our team prioritize which applications to review first.

 - Granola takes notes during our interview calls so our team can focus on the conversation with you.

All hiring decisions are made by humans. Our team reviews applications, conducts interviews, and makes final selections. AI tools assist us but never replace human judgment, and these practices are conducted in compliance with applicable data protection, AI governance, and labor laws. Your data is not used to train AI models.

In accordance with New York City Local Law 144, an independent bias audit has been conducted on "Automated Employment Decision Tools"; results are available for Ashby https://www.ashbyhq.com/downloadables/ashby-bias-audit-08-2024.pdf.

collectedJobs.descriptionText:
We are looking for a Senior Partner Deployed Engineer to join the Customer Solutions team, focused on building Coder’s partner ecosystem across AMER. This is a new function at Coder, modeled on the Forward Deployed Engineer role pioneered by companies like Palantir and now the fastest-growing technical role at frontier AI companies. The difference: instead of embedding with a single customer to deploy a platform, you embed with strategic partners to help them understand, position, and deliver Coder’s platform across their entire customer base.

You are part Field CTO, part Industry Strategist, part Technical Specialist, and part Partner Relations Lead. You will be the technical authority within our AMER partner ecosystem: setting the vision for how Coder fits into each partner’s AI, cloud, and modernization offerings, co-creating the GTM sales plays that partner sellers take to market, building the demonstrations and workshops that generate pipeline, and producing the Partner Relations content that establishes Coder’s technical brand in the ecosystem.

This is not a support role. You are equally comfortable holding a strategic roadmap conversation with a partner CTO and debugging a Kubernetes deployment in a partner’s lab in the same afternoon. You are energized by the challenge of building a new category through partnerships, motivated by the multiplied impact of enabling an entire ecosystem rather than a single customer, and capable of operating with full autonomy in a fast-moving startup environment.

 

What You’ll Do

 - Serve as the strategic technical thought partner to AMER partner leadership, including practice leads, CTOs, and solutions architects at global systems integrators, regional cloud consultancies, and hyperscaler field teams. Own the technical relationship and set the vision for how Coder fits into each partner’s AI and modernization portfolio.

 - Co-create sales plays tailored to each partner’s customer base, vertical focus, and services capabilities. Author Working Backwards outcome proposals for strategic partner-customer combinations that translate AI Development Infrastructure into deal-level urgency.

 - Develop and deliver workshops, Builder Labs, and partner-hosted enablement sessions as the primary awareness and demand generation vehicle for the AMER ecosystem. Build hands-on demonstration environments and interactive experiences that partners can use independently.

 - Intervene directly on the highest-value partner-attached deals across AMER: co-sell calls, technical discovery, PoV scoping, architecture review, and technical win support. Own the engagement until the partner’s team can carry it independently.

 - Transform bespoke partner enablement sessions into structured LMS modules and certification tiers that scale across the AMER partner base without requiring live PDE support for each new partner.

 - Produce “better together” reference architectures for strategic partner combinations across cloud providers and AI platforms. Include deployment diagrams, network topology, IAM patterns, and operational runbooks that partner SAs can hand directly to customers.

 - Codify each successful partner engagement into a repeatable GTM play: trigger conditions, discovery questions, positioning framework, demo script, PoV scope template, and expected outcomes. Build a playbook library that a new PDE or partner seller can pick up and run.

 - Build AI-powered self-service tools that automate high-volume PDE activities: Opportunity Brief Generator, PR/FAQ Generator, Workshop-in-a-Box deployment, and demo site builder.

 - Produce a monthly partner intelligence digest from AMER engagements: what customers are asking for, how competitors are positioning, where integrations are missing, and which vertical use cases are emerging. Distribute to Product, Engineering, and GTM leadership.

 - Own the AMER-relevant portions of the joint technical integration roadmap with strategic partners. Define priorities cross-functionally with Product and Engineering based on field signals from the AMER market.

 - Create and publish Partner Relations content, the ecosystem equivalent of Developer Relations: technical blog posts, cookbooks, partner ecosystem conference talks, enablement videos, and workshop recaps. Build Coder’s technical brand within the AMER partner community.

 - Contribute to cloud marketplace product listing stewardship, competency maintenance documentation, and CSP co-build technical requirements as they apply to AMER -specific partner and compliance contexts.
   
    

What We’re Looking For

 - 7+ years of experience in a combination of Forward Deployed Engineering, Solutions Architecture, Field CTO, Technical Consulting, or Developer Relations roles at an infrastructure, developer tools, or AI company

 - Demonstrated experience helping partners or customers understand and adopt products in emerging or undefined categories, not just executing playbooks for established ones

 - Proven hands-on experience designing and deploying cloud infrastructure on at least one major cloud provider (AWS, Google Cloud, or Microsoft Azure), with production-level Kubernetes and Terraform depth. You have done the work and can speak to it with specificity.

 - 2+ years deploying or operating AI coding agents in a production or near-production environment: you understand how agent loops execute, where credentials live, and what governance and audit requirements look like in an AMER enterprise context

 - Ability to articulate the architectural difference between workspace-local agent tooling and a centralized agentic harness, and to explain why that distinction matters to a security, compliance, or data sovereignty stakeholder

 - Experience working with channel or technology partners in a co-sell model: hyperscaler partner programs, GSI/RSI partnerships, or VAR/distributor ecosystems in AMER markets

 - Experience building repeatable technical GTM assets that scaled beyond your personal delivery: sales plays, enablement curricula, reference architectures, or technical content programs

 - Executive communication and Field CTO credibility: you can hold a technical vision conversation with a partner CTO and a deal-level architecture review with an SE in the same day.

 - Strong written communication: you can produce a Working Backwards PR/FAQ, a technical architecture document, and a blog post without those being separate skills requiring separate people

 - Self-directed, analytically minded, and comfortable operating with full autonomy. You will define processes that don’t exist, build tools that haven’t been scoped, and create a function from first principles in a new region.
   
    

Bonus tacos if you have

(Tacos? Ask us how we say thanks by giving tacos!)

 - Prior Forward Deployed Engineer experience at a platform company (Palantir, Scale AI, frontier AI lab, or equivalent embedded deployment model)

 - Track record of public technical advocacy: blog posts, conference talks, open-source contributions, or developer/partner community engagement

 - Experience with hyperscaler partner programs (e.g., ISV Accelerate, strategic collaboration agreements, co-sell programs) at an operational level

 - Background in AI governance frameworks, session audit requirements, or SIEM integration for AI workloads

 - Experience with LLM gateway or proxy infrastructure (LiteLLM, OpenRouter, or equivalent) in a multi-team or enterprise context

 - Experience designing human-in-the-loop breakpoints or escalation patterns for autonomous agent workflows

 - Kubernetes certification (CKA, CKAD, or CKS)

 - Experience with Tailscale or similar overlay networking tools

 - Open-source contributions, particularly in CNCF, MCP, or AI agent ecosystems
   
    

What Success Looks Like

 - You have done the hard technical work before: deploying cloud-native infrastructure, navigating Kubernetes in production, building with Terraform, and operating in the complexity of large AMER enterprise environments. You bring that credibility into every partner conversation.

 - You can walk a partner CTO through how Coder enables parallelized AI agents in a regulated AMER enterprise, covering credential isolation, audit lineage, GDPR-compliant data handling, and escalation design, and turn that conversation into a joint GTM play their sellers can run next quarter.

 - You can walk into an unstructured partner relationship, assess the technical and commercial opportunity, and chart a path from first enablement session to first co-sourced deal without waiting to be told what to do.

 - You translate deep technical knowledge into assets that scale: reference architectures partners hand to their customers, enablement modules partners consume on their own, and GTM playbooks partner sellers run without PDE involvement.

 - You are as invested in the pattern behind the engagement as you are in the engagement itself. Every bespoke partner interaction produces a reusable artifact. Every field insight feeds back to product. You codify by instinct.

 - You make the ecosystem and the product better: your field experience shapes how Coder builds integrations, how partners deliver, and how the AMER market understands AI Development Infrastructure as a category.

We are looking for a Senior Solutions Engineer, Federal/Public Sector to join our Solutions Engineering team. You will partner with Account Executives to qualify, progress, and close revenue opportunities with civilian, defense, and intelligence community agencies, guiding them through demos, architecture discussions, and proofs-of-concept that prove Coder’s value for both human developers and the AI coding agents working alongside them, often inside classified or air-gapped networks.

This is not a scripted-demo-only role. You are equally comfortable running a deep technical proof-of-concept inside a disconnected or classified environment and stepping back to translate a technical win into a business case a federal decision-maker will act on. You are energized by ambiguity, motivated by winning deals the right way, and capable of bringing the voice of the agency back into how Coder builds and sells.




WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Own the technical relationship with agency prospects through pre-sales, and efficiently manage towards a technical win

 - Lead or support post-sales relationships and renewals when needed

 - Demo the Coder platform from the developer, administrator, and AI agent workflow perspectives, including in classified and air-gapped settings

 - Install Coder on cloud (including GovCloud) and on-prem Kubernetes or VM infrastructure, up to and including air-gapped and disconnected networks

 - Run proofs-of-concept that prove Coder’s value, including for agentic and LLM-powered development workflows, and accelerate deals

 - Evolve into a subject-matter expert on Cloud Development Environments, agentic AI development, and their impact on mission delivery

 - Serve as the agency’s voice, routing insights to Engineering and Product

 - Log feature requests and issues in our public/private Git repositories

 - Troubleshoot Coder deployments, networking, and Kubernetes components during evaluation, including within classified networks

 - Contribute pull requests to Coder’s documentation
   
   


WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR

 - Active TS/SCI clearance with Polygraph required at time of hire; U.S. citizenship required

 - Physically based in the DC / Maryland / Virginia (DMV) area, with ability to travel to customer sites as required

 - Minimum 5 years of experience as a Solutions Engineer selling infrastructure or developer tooling, ideally into federal, defense, or intelligence community customers

 - Experience with AI tooling at both the user level and infrastructure level, including coding agents and assistants (e.g. Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, Cursor) as well as LLM infrastructure such as model proxies and LLM routing layers (e.g. LiteLLM), and the ability to speak credibly to how agencies evaluate and adopt them, including in classified environments

 - Strong customer-facing skills that win trust with technical stakeholders and program offices

 - Ability to translate technical hurdles into mission value in real time

 - Understand agentic AI software development use cases and advocate passionately where appropriate

 - Comfortable leading architecture demos and deep-dive troubleshooting sessions in secure, restricted-access environments

 - Deep Linux fundamentals and comfort at the command line

 - 3+ years hands-on with Docker and Kubernetes

 - Experience with AWS GovCloud, Azure Government, or on-prem/air-gapped Kubernetes deployments

 - 3+ years with Terraform or comparable infrastructure-as-code tooling

 - Solid grasp of networking: ingress controllers, proxies, load balancers, and operating within DoD/IC network boundaries

 - Startup-speed execution, ownership mindset, and a player-coach attitude
   
   


WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

 - You can walk into an ambiguous agency conversation, diagnose the real technical, security, and mission blockers, and design a proof-of-concept that proves value fast, even inside a classified network.

 - You translate deep technical fluency, including on agentic and LLM-based development workflows, into a business case that resonates with program managers, security officers, and mission owners alike.

 - Agencies leave your demos and PoCs with a clear, credible picture of how Coder fits their environment, their developers, and their AI agents, without compromising their security posture.

 - You are as invested in winning the account the right way as you are in closing the current deal; you spot risks early, whether technical, security, or procedural, and loop in the right people.

 - Your field experience feeds back into product and marketing, sharpening how Coder demos and sells into the public sector.
   
   


BONUS TACOS

 - (Tacos? If you need an ice-breaker, ask how we say thanks by giving tacos!)

 - Success at both high-growth startups and larger software vendors

 - Direct experience deploying or supporting AI coding agents in customer environments (e.g. Claude Code, Codex, or similar autonomous/semi-autonomous dev tools)

 - Prior military, intelligence community, or federal civilian service background

 - Experience with FedRAMP, DoD IL4/IL5, or ATO processes

 - Background in CI/CD, DevOps, or developer-platform products

 - Experience in platform engineering or developer platform teams

 - Kubernetes, AWS, or related certifications




ABOUT CODER

Coder is the leading platform for AI development Infrastructure, enabling enterprises to securely run human and AI-driven development workflows in consistent, governed environments. Coder provides self-hosted, agent-ready workspaces that unify developer productivity and platform governance. With Coder, enterprises can confidently evolve from human-only development to AI-assisted and autonomous workflows, without sacrificing security, compliance, or performance. Learn more at coder.com http://coder.com.




INTERVIEW PROCESS 

We believe that the interview process should be transparent, consistent, and enjoyable. We value your time and hope to complete the interview process in two to four weeks, if schedules allow.  Through your interviews, you will meet a mix of individual contributors, managers, and senior leaders. 




AI USE DURING THE INTERVIEW PROCESS

As an AI company, Coder embraces the use of AI tools, and we want to be transparent about our expectations as you navigate our interview process.  

Not permitted: Using AI assistance during conversational interviews.

Permitted: Using AI tooling for take-home assessments. Please flag where and to what extent it was used in your take-home. Your submission will not be penalized for using AI as long as it is done honestly.

collectedJobs.descriptionText:
As a Senior Platform Engineer at Coder, you will own the infrastructure Coder's own engineers build on every day. Our internal environments run the same deployment path we publish for customers, so when something does not hold up at our scale, we find it before a customer does. We avoid building anything so specific to ourselves that a customer could not run the same thing.

Platform Engineering owns three areas. We run the internal environments our engineers develop in, the self-service environments our field teams use to demo Coder, and the release pipeline that publishes every Coder artifact. You will take ownership of components across these and stay accountable for how they behave in production after they ship. Our users are Coder’s engineers and field teams, and you’ll work with them to decide what to build and how we know it worked.




WHAT YOU'LL DO HERE

 - Own one or more components of our Kubernetes platform end to end, from the Terraform and Flux configuration to how they run in production.

 - Improve the platform's observability, so that metrics, logs and alerts land in one stack with a runbook behind every alert.

 - Keep our Kubernetes clusters current, including version and add-on upgrades.

 - Apply cost and performance efficiency to our infrastructure.

 - Work on workspace isolation and container runtimes.

 - Contribute to the release and publishing pipeline for coder/coder, including its workflows, signing and publish targets.

 - Design for least privilege, with short-lived credentials and no shared static keys.

 - Write an RFC when a change warrants one, and a pull request a reviewer can follow without decoding it.

 - Mentor one or two engineers on the components you know best.

 - Run pilots with named users, gather feedback, and measure adoption and time to a useful result (e.g. from request to an environment someone can actually demo on)

 - Own docs, onboarding and support for what you ship.


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - 4+ years in infrastructure or platform engineering, with direct ownership of production systems other people depend on.

 - Strong technical depth across Linux, Kubernetes, containers and Infrastructure as Code, Terraform in particular.

 - Production experience with at least one major public cloud. Most of our infrastructure runs on AWS.

 - Hands-on experience operating Kubernetes clusters, including upgrades, add-ons, autoscaling and the failure modes that come with them.

 - Experience building and owning CI/CD pipelines, and treating them as production software.

 - A working understanding of IP networking and HTTP fundamentals.

 - Has changed or retired a platform feature based on how people used it, or can describe how they would decide to.

 - Good instincts for where cloud spend goes and what a change will cost.

 - Clear written communication. Most of this team's work is agreed in a document before it is built.


BONUS TACOS IF YOU HAVE

 - (Tacos? If you need an ice-breaker, ask how we say thanks by giving tacos!)

 - GitOps at scale with Flux or Argo CD.

 - Prometheus, Grafana or OpenTelemetry, including alerts you defined and owned.

 - Sandboxed container runtimes such as Kata, gVisor or sysbox.

 - Release engineering, artifact signing or supply chain security.

 - Prior work on developer tooling or internal developer platforms.

 - Public open source contributions.

 - You still carve out time to code, either at work or on passion projects.


OUR TECH STACK

 - Backend: Go, Postgres, Kubernetes, gRPC

 - Infrastructure: AWS, Terraform, Flux, Helm

 - Observability: Prometheus, Grafana

 - CI/CD: GitHub Actions

 - General: GitHub, Slack, Discord, Notion

collectedJobs.descriptionText:
Coder is growing from about 220 to 500 people by the end of 2027, and our People team is growing with us. We work in pods (GTM, R&D, G&A), each with its own HRBP and Generalist, so leaders always know who to call.

You'll be the HR partner for our R&D leaders, and the international employment expert for the UK, our Employer of Record (EOR) countries, and APAC. This is a foundational hire for our London entity buildout, and you'll work alongside a London-based Generalist and outside UK counsel.



What you'll do

 - Partner with R&D leaders on performance, org design, employee relations, and people strategy, and flag risks early

 - Advise on international ER and org changes under local law, and know when to bring in outside counsel for high-risk matters such as redundancy and terminations

 - Help build our UK employment infrastructure with Legal and Finance: contracts, probation and notice terms, right to work, statutory leave, policies, and benefits

 - Manage our EOR relationships (Deel, Rippling) and plan the path from EOR to direct employment in key markets

 - Track regulatory changes in the UK and our active EOR countries, including the Employment Rights Act changes, and proactively flag risks

 - Own performance, compensation cycles, promotions, and leveling for the pod with the HR Manager and Total Rewards

 - Build repeatable country playbooks so each new market doesn't start from scratch

 - Keep international employee data accurate in Rippling and Deel, and support audits and reporting
   
   

What we're looking for

 - Located in the Austin metro area or Eastern time zone

 - 5+ years of HRBP experience, including employee relations, with meaningful UK and/or international exposure

 - Strong working knowledge of UK employment law, and familiarity with EOR models and their limitations

 - Hands-on experience with Rippling and/or Deel

 - Detail-oriented enough to catch a contract or comp error before it ships, and strategic enough to know when to escalate

 - Extremely collaborative, working closely with a US- and London-based team
   
   

Bonus tacos if you have

(Tacos? Ask us how we say thanks by giving tacos!)

 - Preferred: SHRM-SCP, SPHR, or equivalent hands-on HR experience

 - Experience supporting a company through a legal entity launch

 - Exposure to APAC or EMEA employment law beyond the UK

 - Experience partnering with engineering or R&D teams in a high-growth SaaS company

As our international footprint grows, this role is expected to grow in scope and strategic ownership.

collectedJobs.descriptionText:
We’re looking for a Staff Software Engineer to help shape AI governance for developer tooling at Coder. This role sits on our AI Governance team, which builds and maintains two enterprise-grade components of Coder's AI governance stack.

AI Gateway is a centralized LLM gateway that sits between coding agents and providers such as OpenAI or Anthropic, providing organizations with audit trails, token tracking, cost control, and centralized authentication. Agent Firewall wraps those agents with default-deny network policies, controlling which domains and methods they can reach inside workspaces.

This team works across the full stack - from Go backend and React frontend to integrating with LLM provider APIs. Day to day, you'll be shipping features, hardening security boundaries, collaborating with enterprise customers on real-world policy needs, and contributing to Coder's open-source ecosystem.

 

What you'll do here

 - Design and build product features that push the standard for remote development in self-hosted environments

 - Create and improve upon popular open source projects that integrate with VS Code, JetBrains, and other developer tools

 - Champion best practices to both internal team members and external contributors

 - Collaborate with Product and Design teams at Coder, as well as with partners like JetBrains, to execute key product integrations

 - Document the design, implementation, and operations of systems for knowledge sharing within the team

 - Work alongside Customer Success teams to support Coder’s enterprise user base

 - Work with cutting-edge AI technologies to create seamless, painless developer experiences

 - Rapidly iterate from prototype to implementation in a highly adaptive, reactive team environment
   
    

What we're looking for

 - 8+ years of full-stack experience writing code in a professional setting, with 1+ year(s) writing Go (ideally in current or most recent position)

 - Proficiency in building distributed systems in Go

 - Excellent verbal and written communication skills

 - Exceptional debugging and troubleshooting skills, and the tenacity to drive a solution to a conclusion

 - You are self-motivated with a creative and analytical mindset

 

Our tech stack

 - Frontend: Typescript, React, Vite

 - Backend: Go, Postgres, GCP, Kubernetes, gRPC

 - Observability: Prometheus, Grafana

 - CI/CD: GitHub Actions

 - General: GitHub, Slack, Discord, Notion

Developers don’t want more marketing. They want relevance, technical depth, and experiences worth showing up for. As Field Marketing Manager you will help bring Coder’s regional marketing programs to life. You will execute field and ABM programs that build awareness, support sales, and create pipeline across the North American market.

You will work closely with a Senior Marketing Manager, sales, partners, and the broader marketing team. You will coordinate events, activate campaigns, and keep programs moving on time and on brand.



What you’ll do here

 - Execute regional field marketing plans aligned to global strategy and North America priorities.

 - Run virtual and in-person events that people actually remember, from platform engineering roundtables to developer meetups to enterprise field programs.

 - Support lead generation and pipeline goals through strategic programs, clear handoffs, and timely follow-through.

 - Partner with global marketing teams to localize campaign content and messaging for North American audiences.

 - Help execute co-branded campaigns and joint event opportunities with strategic alliances, resellers, and channel partners.

 - Partner closely with sales on ABM plays for high-priority accounts, helping turn target account lists into real conversations and pipeline.

 - Coordinate account-specific assets, communications, and campaign touchpoints that support sales outreach and pipeline creation.

 - Support pre-event ABM motions, including target account coordination, personalized outreach support, and follow-up planning.

 - Keep projects organized, timelines moving, and chaos to a minimum across regional campaigns and events.



What we’re looking for

 - Must be located in the New York City metro area

 - 4–7 years of field marketing experience, preferably in B2B technology or developer-focused companies.

 - Hands-on experience executing regional field marketing programs, including events, partner campaigns, and sales-aligned marketing motions.

 - Experience supporting or executing account-based marketing programs, including target account planning, personalized campaign touchpoints, and sales coordination.

 - Strong project management skills with the ability to manage timelines, vendors, details, and cross-functional inputs.

 - Experience partnering closely with sales teams to support pipeline goals and regional priorities.

 - Clear written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to keep stakeholders informed and aligned.

 - Comfort managing multiple programs at once while staying organized, responsive, and detail-oriented.

 - Familiarity with project management tools such as Asana or similar systems.



Bonus tacos if you have

 - Experience marketing to developers, platform engineering teams, DevOps teams, or technical buyers.

 - Experience with enterprise SaaS, cloud infrastructure, open-source, or developer tools.

 - Familiarity with marketing automation, CRM, or ABM platforms such as HubSpot, Salesforce, 6sense or HockeyStack.

 - Experience supporting partner or channel marketing programs.

 - Experience measuring field marketing performance across attendance, engagement, influenced pipeline, and sourced pipeline.

 - Experience supporting a company with an open source offering.



Our tech stack

You do not need to know every tool on day one, but familiarity with common go-to-market systems will help you ramp quickly. This role may work across tools such as Asana, Salesforce, marketing automation platforms, ABM platforms, event platforms, and shared content systems.

The Role

We are looking for a Senior Partner Deployed Engineer to join the Customer Solutions team, focused on building Coder’s partner ecosystem across EMEA. This is a new function at Coder, modeled on the Forward Deployed Engineer role pioneered by companies like Palantir and now the fastest-growing technical role at frontier AI companies. The difference: instead of embedding with a single customer to deploy a platform, you embed with strategic partners to help them understand, position, and deliver Coder’s platform across their entire customer base.

You are part Field CTO, part Industry Strategist, part Technical Specialist, and part Partner Relations Lead. You will be the technical authority within our EMEA partner ecosystem: setting the vision for how Coder fits into each partner’s AI, cloud, and modernization offerings, co-creating the GTM sales plays that partner sellers take to market, building the demonstrations and workshops that generate pipeline, and producing the Partner Relations content that establishes Coder’s technical brand in the ecosystem.

This is not a support role. You are equally comfortable holding a strategic roadmap conversation with a partner CTO and debugging a Kubernetes deployment in a partner’s lab in the same afternoon. You are energized by the challenge of building a new category through partnerships, motivated by the multiplied impact of enabling an entire ecosystem rather than a single customer, and capable of operating with full autonomy in a fast-moving startup environment.



What You’ll Do

 - Serve as the strategic technical thought partner to EMEA partner leadership, including practice leads, CTOs, and solutions architects at global systems integrators, regional cloud consultancies, and hyperscaler field teams. Own the technical relationship and set the vision for how Coder fits into each partner’s AI and modernization portfolio.

 - Co-create sales plays tailored to each partner’s customer base, vertical focus, and services capabilities. Author Working Backwards outcome proposals for strategic partner-customer combinations that translate AI Development Infrastructure into deal-level urgency.

 - Develop and deliver workshops, Builder Labs, and partner-hosted enablement sessions as the primary awareness and demand generation vehicle for the EMEA ecosystem. Build hands-on demonstration environments and interactive experiences that partners can use independently.

 - Intervene directly on the highest-value partner-attached deals across EMEA: co-sell calls, technical discovery, PoV scoping, architecture review, and technical win support. Own the engagement until the partner’s team can carry it independently.

 - Transform bespoke partner enablement sessions into structured LMS modules and certification tiers that scale across the EMEA partner base without requiring live PDE support for each new partner.

 - Produce “better together” reference architectures for strategic partner combinations across cloud providers and AI platforms. Include deployment diagrams, network topology, IAM patterns, and operational runbooks that partner SAs can hand directly to customers.

 - Codify each successful partner engagement into a repeatable GTM play: trigger conditions, discovery questions, positioning framework, demo script, PoV scope template, and expected outcomes. Build a playbook library that a new PDE or partner seller can pick up and run.

 - Build AI-powered self-service tools that automate high-volume PDE activities: Opportunity Brief Generator, PR/FAQ Generator, Workshop-in-a-Box deployment, and demo site builder.

 - Produce a monthly partner intelligence digest from EMEA engagements: what customers are asking for, how competitors are positioning, where integrations are missing, which vertical use cases are emerging. Distribute to Product, Engineering, and GTM leadership.

 - Own the EMEA-relevant portions of the joint technical integration roadmap with strategic partners. Define priorities cross-functionally with Product and Engineering based on field signals from the EMEA market.

 - Create and publish Partner Relations content, the ecosystem equivalent of Developer Relations: technical blog posts, cookbooks, partner ecosystem conference talks, enablement videos, and workshop recaps. Build Coder’s technical brand within the EMEA partner community.

 - Contribute to cloud marketplace product listing stewardship, competency maintenance documentation, and CSP co-build technical requirements as they apply to EMEA-specific partner and compliance contexts.
   
   

What We’re Looking For

 - 7+ years of experience in a combination of Forward Deployed Engineering, Solutions Architecture, Field CTO, Technical Consulting, or Developer Relations roles at an infrastructure, developer tools, or AI company

 - Demonstrated experience helping partners or customers understand and adopt products in emerging or undefined categories, not just executing playbooks for established ones

 - Proven hands-on experience designing and deploying cloud infrastructure on at least one major cloud provider (AWS, Google Cloud, or Microsoft Azure), with production-level Kubernetes and Terraform depth. You have done the work and can speak to it with specificity.

 - 2+ years deploying or operating AI coding agents in a production or near-production environment: you understand how agent loops execute, where credentials live, and what governance and audit requirements look like in a European enterprise context

 - Ability to articulate the architectural difference between workspace-local agent tooling and a centralized agentic harness, and to explain why that distinction matters to a security, compliance, or data sovereignty stakeholder

 - Experience working with channel or technology partners in a co-sell model: hyperscaler partner programs, GSI/RSI partnerships, or VAR/distributor ecosystems in EMEA markets

 - Experience building repeatable technical GTM assets that scaled beyond your personal delivery: sales plays, enablement curricula, reference architectures, or technical content programs

 - Executive communication and Field CTO credibility: you can hold a technical vision conversation with a partner CTO and a deal-level architecture review with an SE in the same day, in English and ideally at least one additional European language

 - Strong written communication: you can produce a Working Backwards PR/FAQ, a technical architecture document, and a blog post without those being separate skills requiring separate people

 - Self-directed, analytically minded, and comfortable operating with full autonomy. You will define processes that don’t exist, build tools that haven’t been scoped, and create a function from first principles in a new region.
   
   

Bonus Points

(Bonus tacos? That’s how we say thanks at Coder. Ask us about it.)

 - Prior Forward Deployed Engineer experience at a platform company (Palantir, Scale AI, frontier AI lab, or equivalent embedded deployment model)

 - Track record of public technical advocacy: blog posts, conference talks, open-source contributions, or developer/partner community engagement

 - Experience with hyperscaler partner programs (e.g., ISV Accelerate, strategic collaboration agreements, co-sell programs) at an operational level

 - Familiarity with European regulatory environments: GDPR, DORA, NIS2, AI Act compliance requirements, and data sovereignty patterns for cloud-native deployments

 - Experience with air-gapped or network-isolated deployments common in European financial services, government, or defense contexts

 - Background in AI governance frameworks, session audit requirements, or SIEM integration for AI workloads

 - Experience with LLM gateway or proxy infrastructure (LiteLLM, OpenRouter, or equivalent) in a multi-team or enterprise context

 - Experience designing human-in-the-loop breakpoints or escalation patterns for autonomous agent workflows

 - Kubernetes certification (CKA, CKAD, or CKS)

 - Experience with Tailscale or similar overlay networking tools

 - Open-source contributions, particularly in CNCF, MCP, or AI agent ecosystems

 - Existing relationships with hyperscaler EMEA solutions architecture teams, European GSI technical practices, or AI infrastructure partner ecosystems

 - Fluency in German, French, or a Nordic language in addition to English
   
   

What Success Looks Like

 - You have done the hard technical work before: deploying cloud-native infrastructure, navigating Kubernetes in production, building with Terraform, and operating in the complexity of large European enterprise environments. You bring that credibility into every partner conversation.

 - You can walk a partner CTO through how Coder enables parallelized AI agents in a regulated European enterprise, covering credential isolation, audit lineage, GDPR-compliant data handling, and escalation design, and turn that conversation into a joint GTM play their sellers can run next quarter.

 - You can walk into an unstructured partner relationship, assess the technical and commercial opportunity, and chart a path from first enablement session to first co-sourced deal without waiting to be told what to do.

 - You translate deep technical knowledge into assets that scale: reference architectures partners hand to their customers, enablement modules partners consume on their own, and GTM playbooks partner sellers run without PDE involvement.

 - You are as invested in the pattern behind the engagement as you are in the engagement itself. Every bespoke partner interaction produces a reusable artifact. Every field insight feeds back to product. You codify by instinct.

 - You make the ecosystem and the product better: your field experience shapes how Coder builds integrations, how partners deliver, and how the EMEA market understands AI Development Infrastructure as a category.

Coder is hiring a Senior Manager, Customer Success Team to build, lead, and scale a high-performing team of Customer Success Managers focused on our enterprise customers. This role will drive customer adoption, retention, expansion, and long-term partnership with some of the world’s most sophisticated engineering organizations.

Coder provides self-hosted software environment and AI development infrastructure that enables enterprises to give developers and AI coding agents a fast, flexible development experience while maintaining the security, governance, and control their organizations require. Our customers span technology, financial services, government, automotive, and other highly regulated industries.

As a leader on the Customer Success team, you will be responsible for developing and coaching a high-performing team, building scalable customer success programs, and ensuring customers achieve measurable value from Coder. You will work closely with Sales, Product, Engineering, and Support to drive adoption, identify opportunities for expansion, and represent the voice of the customer across Coder.

This is a player-coach role. You'll spend most of your time leading and developing the team while remaining directly engaged with strategic customers and helping establish the standard for exceptional enterprise Customer Success.




WHAT YOU'LL DO HERE

 - Lead, mentor, and develop a team of Customer Success Managers to deliver exceptional customer outcomes, retention, and expansion.

 - Own team-level customer success outcomes, including adoption, customer health, ARR, NRR, and overall customer satisfaction.

 - Partner cross-functionally with Sales, Product, Engineering, and Support to drive customer adoption, engagement, retention, and expansion.

 - Develop and execute scalable customer success strategies, processes, playbooks, and metrics for Coder’s growing enterprise customer base.

 - Serve as an executive sponsor for key enterprise accounts, building trusted relationships with senior engineering, platform, infrastructure, security, and technology leaders.

 - Coach the team on executive engagement, strategic account planning, value realization, renewals, and expansion opportunities.

 - Identify customer risks and opportunities across the portfolio and establish proactive strategies to improve adoption, mitigate churn, and increase customer value.

 - Help customers understand and realize the value of Coder across their development organization, including secure development environments and AI-powered software development.

 - Represent the voice of the customer internally, influencing product strategy, roadmap priorities, and operational improvements.

 - Establish a culture of accountability, continuous improvement, and customer obsession across the Customer Success organization.

 - Build the systems, operating rhythms, and reporting needed to scale the team effectively as Coder grows.
   
   


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - 7+ years of experience in Customer Success, Account Management, or related customer-facing roles, with 2+ years leading enterprise Customer Success or Account Management teams.

 - Proven experience working with complex enterprise customers in SaaS, developer tools, cloud infrastructure, AI, cybersecurity, or related technology sectors.

 - Demonstrated track record of driving customer adoption, retention, expansion, and measurable business outcomes.

 - Strong strategic thinking and operational execution skills, with the ability to build frameworks, processes, and programs from the ground up.

 - Exceptional communication and executive presence, with the ability to build trusted relationships with C-suite and senior technical stakeholders.

 - Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to use customer data and insights to identify risks, opportunities, and trends.

 - A coaching mindset and passion for hiring, developing, and building high-performing teams.

 - Ability to operate effectively in a fast-moving, high-growth environment with a high degree of autonomy and ambiguity.

 - Strong technical curiosity and the ability to quickly understand complex products, customer environments, and emerging technologies.

 - Experience partnering cross-functionally with Sales, Product, Engineering, and other teams to drive customer outcomes.
   
   


BONUS TACO IF YOU HAVE 

 - (Tacos? If you need an ice-breaker, ask how we say thanks by giving tacos!)

 - Experience working with developer tools, cloud infrastructure, DevOps, platform engineering, cybersecurity, or AI products.

 - Experience supporting large, global, or highly regulated enterprise organizations.

 - Familiarity with modern software development and infrastructure technologies such as Kubernetes, Terraform, cloud platforms, or developer environments.

 - Experience helping organizations adopt AI coding tools, AI agents, or other emerging AI technologies.

 - Experience working at a high-growth technology company and building Customer Success programs as the organization scales.




ABOUT CODER

Coder is the leading platform for AI development Infrastructure, enabling enterprises to securely run human and AI-driven development workflows in consistent, governed environments. Coder provides self-hosted, agent-ready workspaces that unify developer productivity and platform governance. With Coder, enterprises can confidently evolve from human-only development to AI-assisted and autonomous workflows, without sacrificing security, compliance, or performance. Learn more at coder.com http://coder.com.

We believe that the interview process should be transparent, consistent, and enjoyable. We value your time and hope to complete the interview process in two to four weeks, if schedules allow.  Through your interviews, you will meet a mix of individual contributors, managers, and senior leaders. 




AI USE DURING THE INTERVIEW PROCESS

As an AI company, Coder embraces the use of AI tools, and we want to be transparent about our expectations as you navigate our interview process.

Permitted: Using AI tooling for take-home assessments. Please flag where and to what extent it was used in your take-home. Your submission will not be penalized for using AI as long as it is done honestly.

This is an individual contributor role for someone who thrives in a build-from-scratch environment, knows how enterprise sales work across EMEA, and can move between content creation, regional training, and cross-functional collaboration without losing momentum. You'll work closely with the global enablement team, Marketing, and Product Marketing while independently owning the regional agenda.

 - Identify gaps in the EMEA enablement program and proactively build resources to close them
   
   

What we’re looking for

 - 2–4 years of experience in sales enablement, content creation, or a revenue-facing role with an EMEA focus

 - Strong internal collaborator. You know how to consume global messaging, identify where it needs to flex for the region, and work cross-functionally to get it right

 - Strong problem-solving skills and comfort working through technical ambiguity.

How do you reach people who don't want to be marketed to? You lead with value. That's our approach with developers and the platform and security leaders who buy Coder: ads that speak to the problems they're actually solving, like where their AI agents run, who governs them, and how to keep code and data under their control.

Coder is defining the AI Operating Layer https://coder.com/ai-operating-layer, and paid media is one of the main ways we take that story to market. As our Paid Media Manager, you'll own the strategy and performance of our always-on programs across LinkedIn, Google Search, YouTube, and newer platforms like ChatGPT ads, aimed at our enterprise and target accounts. The goal is better, not just more: every dollar should reach the right people, tell the right story, and turn into pipeline.

You'll direct our paid media agency and give them the Coder context they can't get on their own (ICP, positioning, target accounts, business goals). You're just as comfortable in execution as in strategy. You can audit accounts, fix what's broken, or jump in to launch campaigns, and you know what good looks like down to the platform settings.

You'll report to our Demand Generation lead and work closely with product marketing, design, web, marketing ops, ABM, regional marketing, and GTM engineering.



What you'll do here

 - Own the strategy and performance of our paid channels: LinkedIn (sponsored content, document ads, thought leader ads, video and CTV), Google Search, YouTube, and ChatGPT ads.

 - Lead our paid media agency day-to-day. Set priorities, review launches and ad copy, and hold the work to clear timelines and results.

 - Regularly audit our ad accounts, including campaign structure, settings, audiences, conversion tracking, and spend, and jump in hands-on to build, restructure, or fix campaigns when needed.

 - Own budget allocation, forecasting, and monthly pacing across channels and regions. Recommend where to scale, cut, or pause based on pipeline quality, not just clicks.

 - Run a structured test-and-learn agenda across audiences, keywords and match types, offers, creative, formats, and new channels. Define the hypothesis up front and document what we learn.

 - Build targeting around our ICP and target account lists, including retargeting, exclusion audiences, and intent signals.

 - Tailor programs for NAMER, EMEA, and APAC and for priority verticals like financial services, partnering with regional marketing on what each market needs.

 - Partner with PMM and design to keep ad copy and creative current with our positioning, and share back what's resonating. Work with web on landing pages and conversion paths.

 - Own paid reporting: monthly readouts that connect spend to pipeline and revenue, with a clear point of view on what we should do next.

 - Deliver paid air cover for launches and key moments like AWS re:Invent.
   
   

What we're looking for

 - 5–7 years of paid media or performance marketing experience, including owning multi-channel paid strategy and budgets.

 - Deep hands-on expertise in LinkedIn Campaign Manager and Google Ads (Search and YouTube). You can build, restructure, and audit campaigns yourself, not just review an agency's work.

 - Experience managing agencies or vendors. You hold partners accountable to results and are still someone they want to work with.

 - A track record of owning and scaling meaningful budgets across multiple channels, including pacing, forecasting, and reallocation.

 - Experience leading global paid programs and adjusting strategy to align with each region's priorities and performance.

 - Comfort working with data. You can connect ad platform data with attribution and CRM tools like HockeyStack, HubSpot, or Salesforce, and turn it into decisions.

 - A strong grasp of B2B targeting and measurement: ICP, account lists, segmentation, retargeting, exclusions, and conversion tracking.

 - Strong project management skills across multiple campaigns, deadlines, and stakeholders, and clear communication when things shift.

 - Curiosity about using AI tools and workflows to speed up analysis, reporting, and execution.
   
   

Bonus tacos if you have

 - Experience marketing to developers, platform engineers, or other technical buyers.

 - Experience with ABM or intent tools such as Vector, 6sense, Common Room, or HockeyStack.

 - Experience with emerging or programmatic channels like ChatGPT ads, CTV, StackAdapt, or Reddit.

 - Paid experience from B2C or other industries. We value people who bring ideas from different playbooks.
   
   

Our tech stack

You don't need to know every tool on day one. This role works across LinkedIn Campaign Manager, Google Ads, HockeyStack, HubSpot, Salesforce, GA4, Asana, and AI tools like Claude.

collectedJobs.descriptionText:
We are looking for a Senior Solutions Engineer to join our Sales Engineering team. You will partner with Account Executives to qualify, progress, and close revenue opportunities with Fortune 500 prospects — guiding them through demos, architecture discussions, and proofs-of-concept that prove Coder’s value for both human developers and the AI coding agents working alongside them.

This is not a scripted-demo-only role. You are equally comfortable running a deep technical proof-of-concept and stepping back to translate a technical win into a business case an economic buyer will act on. You are energized by ambiguity, motivated by winning deals the right way, and capable of bringing the voice of the prospect back into how Coder builds and sells.

 

What you will be doing:

 - Own the technical relationship with prospects through pre-sales, and efficiently manage towards a technical win

 - Demo the Coder platform from the developer, administrator, and AI agent workflow perspectives

 - Install Coder on cloud and on-prem Kubernetes or VM infrastructure

 - Run proofs-of-concept that prove Coder’s value including for agentic and LLM-powered development workflows and accelerate deals

 - Evolve into a subject-matter expert on Cloud Development Environments, agentic AI development, and their business impact

 - Serve as the prospect’s and customer’s voice, routing insights to Engineering and Product

 - Track and report product issues and feature requests using Linear

 - Troubleshoot Coder deployments, networking, and Kubernetes components during evaluation

 - Contribute pull requests to Coder’s documentation
   
    

What you bring:

 - Minimum 5 years of experience as a Solutions Engineer selling infrastructure or developer tooling

 - Strong customer-facing skills that win trust with technical stakeholders

 - Ability to translate technical hurdles into business value in real time

 - Understand agentic AI software development use cases and advocate passionately where appropriate

 - Comfortable leading architecture demos and deep-dive troubleshooting sessions

 - Deep Linux fundamentals and comfort at the command line

 - 3+ years hands-on with Docker and Kubernetes

 - Experience with AWS, Google Cloud, or Microsoft Azure

 - 3+ years with Terraform or comparable infrastructure-as-code tooling

 - Solid grasp of networking: ingress controllers, proxies, load balancers

 - Experience with AI tooling at both the user level and infrastructure level  (e.g. Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, Cursor) as well as LLM infrastructure such as model proxies and LLM routing layers (e.g. LiteLLM) and the ability to speak credibly to how enterprises evaluate and adopt them

Not permitted: Using AI assistance during conversational interviews.

Permitted: Using AI tooling for take-home assessments. Please flag where and to what extent it was used in your take-home. Your submission will not be penalized for using AI as long as it is done honestly.

We use AI tools to help manage our recruitment process efficiently and fairly. Specifically:

 - Ashby and Brainerr help us review inbound applications by surfacing candidates who best match the role requirements we've defined. This tool does not make hiring decisions; it helps our team prioritize which applications to review first.

 - Granola takes notes during our interview calls so our team can focus on the conversation with you.

AI tools assist us but never replace human judgment, and these practices are conducted in compliance with applicable data protection, AI governance, and labor laws. Since our founding in 2019, we’ve grown into a diverse team of over 260 - working across Europe and the US, connected by a shared builder spirit and with our centre of gravity in Berlin. Along the way, we’ve:



 - Cultivated a community of more than 650,000 active developers and builders

 - Earned 190K+ GitHub stars, making us one of the world’s Top 40 most popular projects

 - Backed by top investors, from Sequoia’s first German seed to our SAP's recent strategic investment - bringing us to a $5.2bn valuation


That’s the company we’ve built. Now we’d love to see what you can build. If you’re applying, try n8n out - whether you’re technical or not - and share a screenshot of your first workflow with us. The easiest place to start is here: app.n8n.cloud/register http://app.n8n.cloud/register.



We’re in a defining moment of an incredible journey. Come and build with us.

🎯 Your main goal will be to take some of the world's largest organisations from their first n8n deployment to multi-year, seven-figure partnerships, and to help write the playbook for how n8n wins at the very top of the enterprise.

As one of n8n's first Strategic Account Executives, you will own a small portfolio of named accounts drawn from our global top 100. Your portfolio is a deliberate mix: existing customers with clear expansion potential, and greenfield logos where you open the relationship from scratch. This is account-led selling rather than opportunity-led. You run each account like a business, over years rather than quarters.

We are early. The strategic motion is new, and you will shape it alongside a small group of senior sellers and n8n leadership. If you are looking for a fully built territory and a playbook to follow, this is not it. If you want to be one of the people who builds it, read on:


OWN A NAMED PORTFOLIO

 - Build multi-year account plans that map business units, regions, executive sponsors and use cases across large, multi-company groups.

 - Find where n8n already runs inside your accounts and turn that bottom-up adoption into executive-sponsored, company-wide programmes.

 - Open greenfield accounts with research-led outbound to CIOs, CTOs, Heads of AI and platform engineering leaders.


SELL ON BUSINESS VALUE AT EXECUTIVE LEVEL

 - Connect n8n to the board agenda, from AI governance and auditability to efficiency and growth, and lead with outcomes rather than features.

 - Build business cases with real numbers that tie automation and AI agents to each customer's strategic priorities.

 - Multi-thread across engineering, IT, security, risk, finance, legal and procurement, and build champions who sell n8n when you are not in the room.


STRUCTURE, CLOSE AND EXPAND

 - Scope and negotiate multi-year, seven-figure agreements, including enterprise-wide licences, multi-region deployments and deals through system integrators and cloud marketplaces.

 - Run expansion cycles of six to twelve months and greenfield cycles that can stretch longer, through security, legal and global procurement.

 - Partner with Customer Success, Solutions Engineering and Partnerships on our biggest bets, and bring in n8n leadership at the moments that matter.


BUILD THE STRATEGIC MOTION

 - Help define how n8n sells to its largest customers, from deal structures to executive sponsor programmes and expansion playbooks.

 - Take what you learn in the field back to Product, Pricing and leadership.

 - Raise the bar for the AEs around you while staying closest to the customer.


REQUIREMENTS


MUST-HAVES

 - 🏛️ Strategic accounts: You have ten or more years of quota-carrying enterprise software sales experience, including at least three years owning a small named portfolio of strategic, Majors or Global 2000 accounts rather than a broad territory.

 - 💰 Seven-figure deals: You have closed and expanded deals worth €1M+ in total contract value, including multi-year and custom commercial structures, in cycles of six months or more.

 - 🧑‍💼 C-suite credibility: You build relationships with CIOs, CTOs, CFOs and the offices of the COO, and you can talk about their business as well as your product.

 - 📊 Value-based selling: You have built quantified business cases tied to a customer's strategic priorities, and you are ready to walk us through one in detail.

 - 🌱 Land and expand: You have turned one team's adoption into an enterprise-wide commitment and grown accounts across business units or regions.

 - 🎯 Still a hunter: Even with a named portfolio, you create your own pipeline through outbound and executive networking, and you are comfortable with greenfield cycles of 12 to 18 months.

 - 📈 Track record: You have consistently hit or exceeded quota over the past three years.

 - 🧭 Structured selling: You use a methodology such as MEDDPICC and navigate technical evaluations, security reviews, legal and global procurement.

 - 🛠️ Builder mindset: You want to help write the playbook rather than run an existing one, and you already use AI in your daily work.

 - 📍 Location: You are based in Spain, Portugal, Denmark, Finland, Belgium or the Netherlands, you already have the right to work there, and you are comfortable with regular travel to customers across the territory.


NICE-TO-HAVES

 - 🛠️ Technical product background: You have sold developer tools, cloud infrastructure, data, AI, integration or automation platforms.

 - 🤝 Partner-led deals: You have closed deals with global system integrators or through AWS, Azure or Google Cloud marketplaces.

 - 🚀 Open source or PLG exposure: You understand how community adoption turns into enterprise revenue.

 - 🏦 Existing network: You already know senior buyers at large organisations in your territory.

Why join us?

You will take the world's largest organisations from a first n8n deployment to multi-year partnerships, with a product that technical teams already love. You will work closely with Solutions Engineering, Customer Success, Partnerships and Product, and with n8n leadership at the moments that matter, so your voice shapes how we sell at the top of the enterprise. n8n is growing at an exceptional pace, backed by a vibrant community and a remote-first culture built on autonomy, experimentation and high talent density. Apply now and help us bring AI-powered automation to the world's most ambitious companies.About the role

n8n is looking for an Enterprise Account Executive to own and grow a defined enterprise territory across Northern Europe (UK&I, Nordics & Benelux) building pipeline, landing net-new logos, and expanding strategic accounts.

You’ll run a full-cycle, consultative enterprise motion (FTE 2,500+): uncovering technical and business needs, aligning multiple stakeholders, guiding evaluations, and closing high-impact six/seven-figure deals.

This role is ideal for someone who can sell to technical buyers (developers are our ICP), thrives in fast-growing environments, and uses a structured methodology (e.g., MEDDIC/MEDDPICC) to drive predictable outcomes.




WHAT YOU’LL BE DOING

🎯 Own and exceed quarterly and annual revenue targets across a defined Northern Europe enterprise territory

🧭 Build pipeline proactively (≥50%+ sourced by you) through outbound prospecting and smart territory/account planning

🔎 Run deep discovery and qualification using MEDDIC/MEDDPICC—uncovering pain, impact, decision process, decision criteria, and confirming real evidence before you forecast

🧱 Manage the full sales cycle end-to-end: discovery, demos, technical validation/evaluation, proposals, procurement, and negotiations

🧠 Translate technical value into business outcomes—aligning n8n’s automation + AI capabilities to measurable efficiency, risk reduction, and speed-to-delivery

🤝 Orchestrate multi-threaded deals across stakeholders (champions, technical evaluators, security, procurement, and economic buyers) to keep momentum and reduce stall risk

📝 Create and drive mutual action plans with customers—clear next steps, milestones, and shared accountability from first meeting to signature

📈 Maintain rigorous pipeline hygiene, forecast accuracy, and account notes in CRM (Salesforce) communicating clearly and early about risks and next steps

🔗 Partner tightly with Solutions Engineering, SDRs, Marketing, RevOps, and Customer Success to accelerate deals and ensure strong handoffs for expansion

🌍 Represent n8n at events and in-market—building credibility with technical communities and enterprise leaders across Northern Europe (with customer travel as needed)




REQUIREMENTS


MUST-HAVES

🏆 Enterprise SaaS sales track record: 5+ years in quota-carrying roles with consistent overachievement in enterprise segments

🌍 Northern Europe market expertise: Existing network and proven success selling into Northern Europe enterprises (plus relevant languages)

🧩 Complex deal leadership: Proven ability to close multi-stakeholder deals with longer cycles, procurement/legal steps, and high scrutiny

🔎 Methodology-driven execution (MEDDIC/MEDDPICC): You use structured qualification to build high-confidence pipeline and accurate forecasts

🗣️ Executive + technical buyer fluency: You can engage C-level stakeholders and also win credibility with technical audiences (DevOps, SecOps, IT Ops etc.)

🧠 Consultative selling: You lead with customer outcomes, ask sharp questions, and tailor your narrative to the customer’s reality—not a generic pitch

📊 Operational discipline: Strong CRM hygiene, forecast rigor, and a habit of using evidence to drive next steps and internal alignment

🤝 Collaboration mindset: You work smoothly with SE/CS/Marketing/RevOps and elevate the whole deal team, not just your own activity




NICE-TO-HAVES

🧑‍💻 Open-source / community experience: You’ve sold in or alongside open-source ecosystems and understand bottoms-up adoption and PLG signals

🧪 Selling technical workflow/automation products: Experience with integration, API-first platforms, DevOps/SecOps/IT Ops, or adjacent categories

🚀 Early-stage / scale-up experience: You’ve helped build pipeline and playbooks in a fast-growing environment where process is evolving
