Sobre la Oportunidad
Buscamos profesionales con experiencia en comercio exterior y cumplimiento aduanero para participar en un proyecto multilingüe de conocimiento experto enfocado en clasificación arancelaria, regulación aduanera y cumplimiento del comercio internacional en México.
El proyecto consiste en analizar escenarios realistas de importación y exportación, documentar cómo los especialistas toman decisiones regulatorias complejas, desarrollar soluciones de referencia y validar análisis técnicos. Los materiales desarrollados servirán para apoyar el desarrollo y la evaluación de sistemas avanzados de inteligencia artificial orientados a procesos profesionales.
Se trata de una oportunidad flexible de consultoría por proyecto, ideal para profesionales que actualmente ejercen o cuentan con experiencia práctica reciente en comercio exterior y operaciones aduaneras mexicanas.
Tipo de contratación: Consultoría independiente por proyecto (Tiempo parcial y flexible)
Modalidad: Remoto ( México)
Compensación: $ 12/hr

Alcance del trabajo: 10-12 horas semanales.

Responsabilidades
Analizar escenarios realistas relacionados con importaciones y exportaciones conforme a la legislación aduanera mexicana.

Elaborar soluciones de referencia para ejercicios de clasificación arancelaria y cumplimiento regulatorio.

Documentar el razonamiento técnico y normativo que sustenta cada decisión.

Revisar y validar soluciones alternativas desde una perspectiva experta, verificando su precisión técnica y cumplimiento regulatorio.

Identificar información faltante, supuestos incorrectos o secuencias de trabajo inapropiadas.

Referenciar, cuando corresponda, la Ley Aduanera, LIGIE, TIGIE, NOMs, RRNA, T-MEC y demás disposiciones aplicables.

Colaborar con el equipo del proyecto para asegurar que el conocimiento experto quede correctamente documentado.

Requisitos
3 años o más de experiencia práctica reciente en agencia aduanal, clasificación arancelaria, cumplimiento en comercio exterior, operaciones de importación/exportación o áreas relacionadas.

Experiencia práctica vigente o reciente (dentro de los últimos dos años) en operaciones aduaneras mexicanas.

Uno o más de los siguientes perfiles:

Agente Aduanal

Clasificador Arancelario

Especialista en Comercio Exterior

Especialista en Cumplimiento Aduanero

Profesional de Cumplimiento en Importación y Exportación

Consultor en Comercio Exterior

Dominio profesional del español.

Capacidad para explicar y documentar claramente el fundamento técnico y normativo de las decisiones regulatorias y de clasificación.

Se Valorará
Experiencia en uno o más de los siguientes temas:

Clasificación arancelaria

LIGIE / TIGIE

T-MEC

NOMs y RRNA

Valoración aduanera

Reglas de origen

Pedimentos

VUCEM

Auditorías de cumplimiento en comercio exterior

Se valorará experiencia utilizando recursos oficiales como ANAM, SAT, SNICE o VUCEM. La experiencia con plataformas comerciales de comercio exterior es bienvenida, pero no es un requisito.

Inglés funcional para comprender instrucciones del proyecto y comunicarse con el equipo.

También se valorará conocimiento de la normativa aduanera de Estados Unidos, clasificación HTS o procesos de comercio transfronterizo entre México y Estados Unidos.

Por Qué es Importante este Proyecto?
Su experiencia contribuirá a documentar cómo los profesionales del comercio exterior y las aduanas resuelven, en la práctica, problemas regulatorios complejos. Al capturar los flujos de trabajo y los procesos de toma de decisiones de expertos, contribuirá al desarrollo de materiales de referencia de alta calidad que respaldan sistemas avanzados de inteligencia artificial multilingües para aplicaciones profesionales en cumplimiento aduanero y comercio internacional.

About the Project
Project Hydrus is a scripted and conversational audio data collection project. The recordings produced help build natural, everyday-sounding synthesized voices for conversational AI products — voices that sound like real people talking, not scripted performances.
As Session Director, you'll lead live recording sessions with Voice Contributors, guiding them through scripted scenarios to produce natural, conversational-quality audio. This hands-on role blends creative direction, coaching, and technical audio judgment — making scripted material sound authentic and unscripted, rather than recited, while keeping sessions moving at a natural pace.
What You'll Do
- Direct voice performers through scripted scenarios, coaching for natural, conversational delivery rather than verbatim recitation.
- Build quick scene context for performers (who, where, why) and improvise to fill narrative or dialogue gaps live, keeping sessions flowing naturally.
- Adapt scripted wording for natural phrasing and regional/dialect authenticity as needed.
- Monitor and correct technical audio quality in real time: mic technique, pacing, clarity, and background noise.
- Manage session pacing to meet recording targets without sacrificing performance quality, and maintain organized notes on adjustments and retakes.
- Create a supportive, low-pressure environment for performers, including those with limited prior voice experience.
What We're Looking For
Required
- Native fluency in the required language (with specific dialect), with a strong ear for natural, colloquial phrasing.
- Experience directing, coaching, or producing voice or audio talent (e.g., voice direction, casting direction, audio/podcast production, dubbing/ADR, or theater direction).
- Demonstrated ability to give clear, specific, actionable performance direction.
- Strong working knowledge of basic recording/mic technique (proximity, plosives, room noise, levels).
- Comfortable improvising and adjusting scripted material on the spot.
- Excellent interpersonal skills; able to build rapport quickly with performers of varying experience levels.
Preferred (nice to have, not required)
- Background in improv, theater direction, or acting coaching.
- Experience directing non-professional or first-time voice talent specifically.
- Familiarity with DAWs or recording software (e.g., Pro Tools, Adobe Audition, Reaper) for spot-checking audio quality.

Commitment & Compensation
- Estimated time: Approximately 8 hours calibration, plus supervision across two recording sessions of ~4 hours each per participant
- Work Type - Freelance Remote

Welo Global is a leader in multilingual AI, technology, and content solutions serving over 2,000 clients in 300 languages. The company combines globally scaled multilingual infrastructure, including a network of over 500,000 linguists and domain experts, with advanced NLP, computational linguistics, and best-in-class compliance backed by seven ISO certifications. Welo Global’s five brands—Welocalize (multilingual content and localization services for global enterprises), Park IP (intellectual property and patent translation services for law firms and corporate legal teams), Welo Life Sciences (regulated language and compliance-aligned content solutions for pharmaceutical, biotech, and medical device organizations), Adapt (multilingual performance-led digital marketing agency), and Welo Data (multilingual data generation, evaluation, and human data infrastructure for AI systems)—serve distinct customer segments with purpose-built expertise, fit-for-purpose solutions, and supporting technology. weloglobal.com
To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
ROLE OVERVIEW
Welo Global is partnering with a social media client to build high-quality training data for AI systems. We are looking for Brazilian experts to help create challenging, expert-level questions and answers in their field. The content that will directly shape how AI understands Brazilian culture, law, history, and society.
This is a remote, flexible freelance engagement. All work is done in Brazilian Portuguese.
What you'll do
For each assignment, you will craft a challenging, expert-level question on a Brazilian topic in your field (one that AI tools cannot fully answer), write the ideal response in Brazilian Portuguese and break that response down into individually cited facts with their sources and relevance.
Important: AI tools may be used for research support only. All questions, answers, and fact breakdowns must be your own original work.
We are looking for experts in the domain listed in the job posting.
Project details
Language Pair: Brazilian Portuguese
Task: AI data annotation
Area of expertise (domain): Fandoms (Music, Pop, Disney & Political Memes)
Tools: Consumer-grade LLM with search (e.g., Gemini Pro), for prompt difficulty calibration
Estimated Volume: 60 hours over approximately 2 months, the hours are flexible, work on your own schedule
Location: Remote
Engagement Type: Freelance / Independent Contractor
If this opportunity aligns with your experience, we would be happy to receive your application.

Share an updated CV
A brief overview of your relevant experience, particularly in Fandoms (Music, Pop, Disney & Political Memes) and how many years you have worked in the field
Your current availability and estimated monthly capacity
Thank you again for your interest in working with Welo Global. I look forward to learning more about your profile and exploring a potential collaboration.
Beware of recruitment scams. Welo Global and all of its brands never recruit through direct messages on social media or WhatsApp, and never asks candidates to pay money for a job. Be wary of unexpected offers, generic email addresses (such as Gmail or Yahoo), and requests for fees or sensitive information. Report suspicious messages and learn more: Recognizing Scams and Confirming Legitimate Welocalize Communications – Welo Global

collectedJobs.descriptionText:
About the Project
Project Hydrus is a scripted and conversational audio data collection project. We're looking for native-level speakers who can deliver natural, everyday-sounding speech — recordings that hold up whether you're reading a script or speaking spontaneously.
Please note: the recordings you produce may be used to create synthesized, AI-generated voices for conversational AI products. Full details on how your data is collected, used, shared, and retained are set out in a Consent Form, which you'll review and sign before any paid session recording begins
What You'll Do If Selected:
Two supervised sessions of approximately 4 hours each, guided in real time by a Session Director on a separate recording platform.
Record scripted material in a natural, conversational tone — faithfully, without a polished, performed, or “announcer” delivery.
Record unscripted, spontaneous speech on a given topic, matching the same warmth and pace as your scripted takes.
Set up and manage your own recording space and equipment for session recording.
Deliver all recordings entirely in the required language (with specific dialect), without code-switching into other languages or dialects.
What We're Looking For

Required
Experience as a voice actor, actor, or theater performer, or a comparable performance background.
Native or native-equivalent fluency in the required language (with specific dialect).
Access to a quiet recording space, free of echo and background noise (acoustically treated for session recording, if selected).
Owns or will acquire a dedicated, professional-grade microphone for the audition (e.g. RODE NT-USB Mini, Blue Yeti), upgrading to a qualifying USB condenser or XLR mic + audio interface for session recording if selected. Built-in laptop mics, AirPods, earbuds, and headsets are not accepted at any stage.
Owns closed-back monitoring headphones (required for session recording if selected).
Comfortable both self-directing for the audition and taking live direction from a Session Director in guided sessions.
Preferred (nice to have, not required)
Professional voice-over experience (dubbing/ADR, audiobook, podcasting) in a conversational rather than commercial/announcer register.
Baseline audio hygiene: comfortable setting mic distance and catching noise, clipping, or distortion yourself.
An existing home recording setup already treated for sound.

Your Data & Privacy

Before any session recording, you'll be asked to review and sign a Consent Form covering how your voice recordings are collected, used (including to train synthesized/AI voice models), shared with approved partners, retained, and how to exercise your data rights (access, correction, deletion, and more, depending on where you live). If you'd like to review these terms before applying, contact us and we'll share a copy in advance.

必須条件
高い日本語力

日本のポピュラーカルチャーに関する十分な知識
信頼性の高いコンピューターシステムと安定したインターネット環境

機密を保護するための機密保持契約書（NDA）およびサービスレベル契約（SLA）への署名

Join a short, paid project that tests whether AI coding agents work as well on instructions written in the target language as they do in English. Your language skills and technical background decide where you fit.
About the project
Welo Data is helping evaluate how well AI coding agents perform when the instructions they receive are written in languages other than English. Agents are given a real software engineering task in a code repository, and automated tests check whether they solved it. The code, repositories and tests stay exactly as they are. Only the human-written instructions change language, so the quality of every instruction directly affects the result.
About the roles
There are two roles on this project. We place you in one of them based on your experience& skillsets.
Translator: translate English software engineering task briefs into the target language. You keep every requirement, constraint and success condition, and you leave commands, file paths, API names, code and test conditions exactly as written in English. This role suits people with a stronger technical background, and translation experience is a plus.

About Welocalize
Welocalize, a Welo Global brand, serves localization teams through AI-enabled multilingual content solutions that enable enterprises to operate and scale globally. Welocalize combines AI, automation, and human expertise to support enterprises in more than 300 languages, enabling accurate, culturally aligned, and compliant multilingual content at scale.

Welocalize’s Opal Platform comprises patented technology designed to automate multilingual content and improve workflow performance for enterprises. Opal functions as an agentic system that orchestrates AI, automation, and human expertise to coordinate content workflows across the lifecycle, improving speed, scalability, and operational control for global enterprises. These solutions operate within a secure and compliant environment supported by seven ISO certifications. Welocalize is headquartered in New York with offices worldwide. welocalize.com

MAIN PURPOSE OF JOB

The Polish Linguist role involves managing translation and copy-editing tasks, ensuring high-quality linguistic deliverables for assigned projects or accounts. Responsibilities include coordinating with freelancers and agencies, maintaining language resources, resolving terminology queries, and collaborating with clients and internal teams to enhance workflow efficiency.
Please note that in order to do this job is important to be located and to have the legal right to work in one of the following countries: Spain, Italy, Romania, Greece, Germany.

MAIN RESPONSABILITIES
The following is a non-exhaustive list of responsibilities and areas of ownership for this role:

Performing copy-edit tasks on assigned projects or accounts

Performing on-demand translation tasks

Performing lead support on assigned projects or accounts

Managing and maintaining the language materials (including glossaries, Style Guides, work instruction) up to the quality standards and up to date as required by the account or project

Managing project-related queries

Ensuring good interaction among team members and resolving questions on terminology and language matters

Testing and qualifying new freelancers and vendors as required

Developing and training of internal linguists and external partners according to the accounts’ and Welocalize’s needs

Interacting with clients on linguistic matters as required

Participating in the development of new and improved working processes

Meet or exceed the KPIs in terms of productivity, on time delivery, quality

Achieving the goals set by the team manager

REQUIREMENTS
Education

University degree in Translation/Applied Languages/Linguistic Studies or equivalent combination of education and experience (University degree in other fields plus 2 years of full time experience in translation; OR 5 years of full time professional experience in translating)

Experience

Native-level fluency in the Polish language

Fluency in English, both written and spoken in a variety of registers

4+ years of experience in translation/localization/editing or content writing

2+ years of review experience

Thorough understanding of the localization process.

Good user experience of standard software, such as Windows and Office applications.

Good user experience of standard CAT tools, e.g., XTM, SDL Studio, and issue tracking and query management tools, e.g. JIRA

Ability to learn new localization tools and applications quickly.

Excellent interpersonal, written, and verbal communication skills.

Excellent knowledge of terminology used in two or more subject matters.

Ability to work with tight deadlines.

Ability to give clear, concise, and constructive feedback.

Ability to effectively present information and respond to questions from groups of managers, clients, customers, and linguists

Ability to solve practical problems and deal with a variety of concrete variables in situations where only limited standardization exists. Ability to interpret a variety of instructions furnished in written, oral, diagram, or schedule form.

Ability and willingness to train/teach others and pass on knowledge.

Ability, willingness, and experience in communicating positively with customers at various levels

Ability to work within a virtual team

Overview
Welo Data is looking for sharp, curious, and detail-oriented individuals to join our team as Data Labeling Associate.
This is not a traditional annotation role.
You’ll be working directly with cutting-edge AI systems — evaluating outputs, identifying gaps, and helping improve how these systems behave in real-world scenarios. The work sits at the intersection of data quality, model evaluation, and human judgment, where your ability to think critically matters just as much as following guidelines.
We’re looking for people who are naturally curious about AI, comfortable forming opinions, and confident in contributing to conversations with teammates, leads, and stakeholders.

Naturally curious about AI, technology, and how systems behave

About the Project
Project Hydrus is a scripted and conversational audio data collection project. The recordings produced help build natural, everyday-sounding synthesized voices for conversational AI products — voices that sound like real people talking, not scripted performances.
As Session Director, you'll lead live recording sessions with Voice Contributors, guiding them through scripted scenarios to produce natural, conversational-quality audio. This hands-on role blends creative direction, coaching, and technical audio judgment — making scripted material sound authentic and unscripted, rather than recited, while keeping sessions moving at a natural pace.
What You'll Do
- Direct voice performers through scripted scenarios, coaching for natural, conversational delivery rather than verbatim recitation.
- Build quick scene context for performers (who, where, why) and improvise to fill narrative or dialogue gaps live, keeping sessions flowing naturally.
- Adapt scripted wording for natural phrasing and regional/dialect authenticity as needed.
- Monitor and correct technical audio quality in real time: mic technique, pacing, clarity, and background noise.
- Manage session pacing to meet recording targets without sacrificing performance quality, and maintain organized notes on adjustments and retakes.
- Create a supportive, low-pressure environment for performers, including those with limited prior voice experience.
What We're Looking For
Required
- Native fluency in the required language (with specific dialect), with a strong ear for natural, colloquial phrasing.
- Experience directing, coaching, or producing voice or audio talent (e.g., voice direction, casting direction, audio/podcast production, dubbing/ADR, or theater direction).
- Demonstrated ability to give clear, specific, actionable performance direction.
- Strong working knowledge of basic recording/mic technique (proximity, plosives, room noise, levels).
- Comfortable improvising and adjusting scripted material on the spot.
- Excellent interpersonal skills; able to build rapport quickly with performers of varying experience levels.
Preferred (nice to have, not required)
- Background in improv, theater direction, or acting coaching.
- Experience directing non-professional or first-time voice talent specifically.
- Familiarity with DAWs or recording software (e.g., Pro Tools, Adobe Audition, Reaper) for spot-checking audio quality.

Commitment & Compensation
- Estimated time: Approximately 8 hours calibration, plus supervision across two recording sessions of ~4 hours each per participant
- Work Type - Freelance Remote
- Rate: $50.00 USD per hour

About the Opportunity
We are seeking experienced customs and trade compliance professionals to support a project focused on Mexican import/export regulations, tariff classification, and customs compliance.
This project involves reviewing realistic customs scenarios, documenting how experienced professionals approach complex regulatory decisions, developing expert reference solutions, and validating technical analyses. The resulting expert materials will support the development and evaluation of advanced AI systems for professional workflows.
This is flexible, project-based consulting work intended for professionals who are actively practicing or have recent hands-on experience in Mexican customs and trade compliance.
Project Details:-
Engagement Type: Independent Contractor / Project-Based (Flexible, Part-Time)
Location:Remote (Mexico)
Compensation: $12/hr

Scope of work: 10 hrs-12 hrs Weekly

What You’ll Do
Review realistic import and export scenarios involving Mexican customs regulations.

Develop expert reference solutions for customs classification and trade compliance tasks.

Document the reasoning behind customs decisions and regulatory interpretations.

Review and validate alternative solutions for technical accuracy, completeness, and regulatory compliance.

Identify missing information, incorrect assumptions, or inappropriate decision sequences.

Reference applicable regulations where appropriate (e.g., Ley Aduanera, LIGIE, TIGIE, NOMs, RRNA, T-MEC).

Collaborate with our project team to ensure expert knowledge is accurately represented.

Required Qualifications
3+ years of recent, hands-on experience in customs brokerage, tariff classification, trade compliance, import/export operations, or a related field.

Current or recent (within the past two years) practical experience with Mexican customs regulations and procedures.

One or more of the following professional backgrounds:

Licensed Agente Aduanal

Clasificador Arancelario

Trade Compliance Specialist

Customs Compliance Specialist

Import/Export Compliance Professional

Customs or Trade Consultant

Professional fluency in Spanish.

Ability to clearly explain and document the reasoning behind regulatory and classification decisions.

Preferred Experience
Experience in one or more of the following areas is highly desirable:

Tariff classification (Clasificación Arancelaria)

LIGIE / TIGIE

T-MEC / USMCA

NOMs and RRNA

Customs valuation

Rules of origin

Pedimentos

VUCEM

Customs audits or trade compliance reviews

Experience using official Mexican customs resources (e.g., ANAM, SAT, SNICE, VUCEM) is preferred. Experience with commercial customs software is welcome but not required.

Working proficiency in English sufficient to understand project instructions and communicate with the project team.

Knowledge of U.S. customs regulations, HTS classification, or cross-border Mexico-U.S. trade operations is a plus.

Why This Project Matters?
Your expertise will help document how experienced customs professionals solve complex regulatory problems in practice. By capturing expert workflows and decision-making, you will contribute to the development of high-quality reference materials that support advanced AI systems for professional customs and trade compliance.

About Welo Global
Welo Global is a leader in multilingual AI, technology, and content solutions serving over 2,000 clients in 300 languages. The company combines globally scaled multilingual infrastructure, including a network of over 500,000 linguists and domain experts, with advanced NLP, computational linguistics, and best-in-class compliance backed by seven ISO certifications. Welo Global’s five brands—Welocalize (multilingual content and localization services for global enterprises), Park IP (intellectual property and patent translation services for law firms and corporate legal teams), Welo Life Sciences (regulated language and compliance-aligned content solutions for pharmaceutical, biotech, and medical device organizations), Adapt (multilingual performance-led digital marketing agency), and Welo Data (multilingual data generation, evaluation, and human data infrastructure for AI systems)—serve distinct customer segments with purpose-built expertise, fit-for-purpose solutions, and supporting technology. weloglobal.com

Job Overview
Ready to shape how people learn in the age of AI? We’re looking for an experienced Instructional Designer to join our L&D team and help us create learning with Sana, our AI-powered content development tool.
You’ll combine instructional expertise with AI fluency to turn expert knowledge and existing materials into clear, interactive, scalable learning experiences. AI handles much of the manual production. You guide it, direct it, and make sure everything that reaches our learners is accurate, purposeful, and on standard.
This role is based in India, and you’ll collaborate daily with colleagues across locations and time zones.
Main Responsibilities
Design learning with AI
Create courses and learning experiences in Sana, using it to draft outlines, learning objectives, lesson content, summaries, and assessments
Turn existing materials, such as slide decks, PDFs, SOPs, and technical documentation, into engaging interactive learning
Write effective prompts and instructions, and refine AI outputs until they meet instructional, technical, and brand standards
Use AI to adapt content for different roles, regions, and languages, and keep it current as processes and client requirements change
Explore new AI capabilities, share what works with the team, and help shape our standards for AI-enabled content development
Apply human expertise where it matters most
Partner with subject matter experts to identify business, client, and learner needs, and to validate content before it’s published
Review all AI-generated content for technical accuracy, tone, quality, and compliance with in-house standards and client guidelines. You are the final quality checkpoint
Translate complex technical information into clear language while keeping it accurate
Set clear instructional goals and make sure every piece of content helps learners achieve them
Build, measure, and improve
Develop learning content that meets our LMS requirements, including SCORM packages where needed
Design assessments and use learner data and feedback to improve both the content and the learner experience
Create supporting media (audio, visuals, simulations) that strengthen learning, using AI-assisted tools where appropriate
Work with operational leaders to support the ongoing monitoring and mentoring of learners
Collaborate and scale
Work with cross-functional teams across remote and office-based locations

About Welo Global
Welo Global is a leader in multilingual AI, technology, and content solutions serving over 2,000 clients in 300 languages. The company combines globally scaled multilingual infrastructure, including a network of over 500,000 linguists and domain experts, with advanced NLP, computational linguistics, and best-in-class compliance backed by seven ISO certifications. Welo Global’s five brands—Welocalize (multilingual content and localization services for global enterprises), Park IP (intellectual property and patent translation services for law firms and corporate legal teams), Welo Life Sciences (regulated language and compliance-aligned content solutions for pharmaceutical, biotech, and medical device organizations), Adapt (multilingual performance-led digital marketing agency), and Welo Data (multilingual data generation, evaluation, and human data infrastructure for AI systems)—serve distinct customer segments with purpose-built expertise, fit-for-purpose solutions, and supporting technology. weloglobal.com

About the Role
We're hiring a technically strong Senior Data Analyst to help modernize how our FP&A organization uses data, analytics, and automation. This is an embedded Finance role: you'll report directly to the FP&A Director and work side by side with her day to day while partnering closely with our central Data Analytics and Data Engineering teams on infrastructure, standards, and complex technical problems. It's a hands-on execution role for someone who builds.
Financial and operational data at Welocalize lives across multiple systems - Workday Financials, Adaptive Planning, Salesforce, a Redshift data warehouse, Power BI, and years of Excel workbooks carrying critical processes. Much of it doesn't connect cleanly, and a lot of institutional knowledge lives in undocumented spreadsheets, manual processes, and Power Queries rather than any system of record.
You might start with a complex, years-old Excel workbook and a simple prompt: “This is how we do this today.” Your job isn't to automate the workbook as-is - it's to understand its purpose, trace its logic to source, figure out what users actually need, and design something better: a rebuilt pipeline, a SQL/Python replacement, a driver-based view, an exception-monitoring workflow, or an AI-assisted tool.
We're just starting to build out an FP&A AI repository - documentation, business logic, and workflows meant to let AI reliably execute FP&A processes, not just answer one-off questions - and you'll partner with us to determine its direction.
This role is a deliberate combination of three things:
1. Fluency with data itself - the ability to query, shape, and manipulate data directly.
2. An engineering mindset - building automated, repeatable systems (workflows and dashboards that run and refresh on their own, integrations across tools) rather than one-off analysis, and knowing how to scope and coordinate real pipeline or data mart work with Data Engineering.
3. An investigative instinct - the ability to look at data and figure out what it's telling us, not just execute a report exactly as specified.

What You'll Do
Partner directly with FP&A leadership to understand existing reporting, analytical, and planning processes and identify where they should fundamentally change, not just get faster.

• Reverse-engineer complex Excel workbooks and manual processes to understand their data sources, business logic, calculations, and the questions their users are actually trying to answer.

• Design and build automated solutions using SQL, Python, ETL/data transformation, APIs, and modern AI tools.

• Work through large, imperfect, multi-system datasets - resolving data quality, mapping, reconciliation, and grain issues along the way.

• Perform exploratory analysis to identify trends, anomalies, relationships, and underlying business drivers, rather than simply reporting what happened.

• Design dashboards and reporting experiences around the decisions people actually need to make, not a recreation of an existing spreadsheet in a new tool.

• Build AI-assisted, interactive HTML reporting tools - developed with the help of AI coding tools and engineered to refresh efficiently on their own, without repeated AI calls.

• Develop driver-based analysis, exception reporting, and monitoring approaches that surface important changes proactively.

• Explore and build AI-assisted and agentic workflows - including ways for LLMs to interact with data, tools, APIs, and reporting processes.

• Partner with the central Data Analytics and Data Engineering teams on shared data infrastructure and standards - including scoping and coordinating data pipeline and data mart requests.

• Contribute in a leadership capacity within the analytics function even without formal management responsibility - shaping how problems get approached, mentoring by example, and helping set the bar for analytical rigor.

• Translate complex analytical findings into clear, actionable insight for Finance leaders and other business stakeholders.

• Partner in building out our FP&A AI repository - the documentation, conventions, and workflows meant to let an AI assistant execute FP&A processes reliably - and help shape its direction as we go.

How You Think
Technical skills matter, but how you approach problems matters just as much. We're looking for someone who:

• Is genuinely curious and naturally asks “why?” when something doesn't reconcile or doesn't make sense.

• Enjoys digging into messy or unfamiliar data and figuring out how things connect.

• Doesn't assume an existing process or report is right simply because that's how it's always been done.

• Can take an ambiguous problem and independently structure an approach to solving it, while knowing when to pull others in rather than spinning wheels alone.

• Looks beyond the initial request to identify opportunities, risks, and better approaches the requester may not have thought to ask for.

• Enjoys collaborative problem-solving - bouncing ideas around, testing hypotheses, and challenging assumptions to get to a stronger answer.

• Takes ownership of the areas they work in - the business purpose, the data, the known issues, and the opportunities for improvement - rather than treating each request as a one-off ticket.

• Likes building things, experimenting, and continuously improving how work gets done.

Required Skills and Experience
5-10 years of relevant experience required. You should be genuinely, hands-on strong across:

• SQL - comfortable joining tables, tracing grain, finding duplicates, and validating results in unfamiliar schemas.

• Python - practical proficiency for data transformation, analysis, and automation.

• ETL/ELT fluency - strong enough understanding of pipeline design to define data requirements, validate output, and partner effectively with Data Engineering on pipeline and data mart requests. Hands-on pipeline-building experience is a plus.

• Report and dashboard building - able to design and build a reporting/analytical experience end-to-end, whether on a modern BI platform (Power BI, Tableau, Looker, or similar) or as a standalone interactive HTML/web-based report. Standalone HTML/web-based reports are increasingly our primary format.

• Automation - demonstrated experience automating manual, recurring data or reporting workflows.

• Comfort learning and adopting new AI-assisted tools and workflows - you should be genuinely curious about this space and ready to build fluency quickly on the job.

• Advanced Excel, including the ability to deconstruct sophisticated, undocumented legacy workbooks.

• Demonstrated ability to explore data and figure out why something happened - forming and testing your own hypotheses, not just reporting what happened.

• Fluent English, spoken and written. This is a fully remote role and you'll communicate directly, in English, with business stakeholders and executive leadership as well as data analysts and engineers across our global organization, where English is the shared working language.

Preferred Experience
Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Data Science, or a related quantitative/technical field strongly preferred; equivalent experience acceptable. Master's degree is a plus.

• Experience supporting Finance, FP&A, Strategy, Operations, or another analytically intensive business function.

• Familiarity with financial concepts such as revenue, margin, profitability, forecasting, and variance analysis.

• Experience modernizing legacy Excel-based reporting or analytical processes.

• Experience working in an environment where data is distributed across multiple systems and isn't always perfectly documented.

• Experience working effectively in a fully remote, distributed team environment.

• Exposure to AI/agentic tooling, or experience helping design how AI gets applied to a business process (e.g., LLM workflows, tool/function calling, RAG, MCP, building AI-assisted reporting or automation).

• Machine learning, statistical modeling, or formal data science experience is welcome but not required.

You will own the locale’s interpretation of the client’s quality standards and make sure that the Post-Editing Lead, Post Editors, and Reviewers all work to the same shared understanding of “good”. You will be the main point of contact for the client’s Language Manager on quality discussions, arbitration, and escalations, and you will drive consistency, quality governance, and continuous improvement across UI, marketing, product, informational, legal, and support content.
Project Details
- Location: Remote (based in one of the approved countries below)
- Expected volume: Approximately 24 hours per month
- Employment type: Freelance / Independent Contract
- Task type: Language Lead Support
- Content types: UI, Marketing, Informational, Legal, Product, Support

What You Will Do
-Analyse requirements: Review every style guide and glossary update, assess which quality categories and content types it affects, and record the changes. Track what the client’s Language Manager actually corrects and says in calibration and quality calls, not only what is written down.
-Relay expectations: Run regular alignment roundtables with the language community and publish a structured monthly quality digest covering performance, priority improvement areas, style guide updates, and notable errors and arbitration outcomes.
-Manage review quality actively: Coach Reviewers one-to-one using specific examples, run shadowing sessions from real alignment data.
-Improve the standard: Turn recurring justification patterns into well-reasoned style guide proposals, and share cross-locale patterns with the Welocalize Quality Manager.
-Maintain alignment with the client: Treat Language Manager decisions as the standard, raise concerns with evidence at the right forum, and aim for fewer surprises over time.

-The community’s shared understanding of quality
-The integrity of the arbitration record, ensuring that every arbitration sent to the client is valid and well-evidenced
-The working relationship with the client’s Language Manager, including clarifications, escalations, and expectation tracking
Requirements

About Welo Global
Welo Global is a leader in multilingual AI, technology, and content solutions serving over 2,000 clients in 300 languages. The company combines globally scaled multilingual infrastructure, including a network of over 500,000 linguists and domain experts, with advanced NLP, computational linguistics, and best-in-class compliance backed by seven ISO certifications. Welo Global’s five brands—Welocalize (multilingual content and localization services for global enterprises), Park IP (intellectual property and patent translation services for law firms and corporate legal teams), Welo Life Sciences (regulated language and compliance-aligned content solutions for pharmaceutical, biotech, and medical device organizations), Adapt (multilingual performance-led digital marketing agency), and Welo Data (multilingual data generation, evaluation, and human data infrastructure for AI systems)—serve distinct customer segments with purpose-built expertise, fit-for-purpose solutions, and supporting technology. weloglobal.com

The Role
We are seeking an experienced English into Slovak Review Lead to serve as the language quality owner and primary client-facing linguistic expert for a leading global technology client.
You will own the locale’s interpretation of the client’s quality standards and make sure that the Post-Editing Lead, Post Editors, and Reviewers all work to the same shared understanding of “good”. You will be the main point of contact for the client’s Language Manager on quality discussions, arbitration, and escalations, and you will drive consistency, quality governance, and continuous improvement across UI, marketing, product, informational, legal, and support content.
Project Details
- Location: Remote (based in one of the approved countries below)
- Expected volume: Approximately 24 hours per month
- Employment type: Freelance / Independent Contract
- Task type: Language Lead Support
- Content types: UI, Marketing, Informational, Legal, Product, Support
- Language pair: English into Slovak (Slovakia)
What You Will Do
-Analyse requirements: Review every style guide and glossary update, assess which quality categories and content types it affects, and record the changes. Track what the client’s Language Manager actually corrects and says in calibration and quality calls, not only what is written down.
-Relay expectations: Run regular alignment roundtables with the language community and publish a structured monthly quality digest covering performance, priority improvement areas, style guide updates, and notable errors and arbitration outcomes.
-Manage review quality actively: Coach Reviewers one-to-one using specific examples, run shadowing sessions, and deliver training built from real alignment data.
-Improve the standard: Turn recurring justification patterns into well-reasoned style guide proposals, and share cross-locale patterns with the Welocalize Quality Manager.
-Maintain alignment with the client: Treat Language Manager decisions as the standard, raise concerns with evidence at the right forum, and aim for fewer surprises over time.
What You Will Own
-The locale’s review service score, including RQE audit and alignment performance
-The community’s shared understanding of quality
-The integrity of the arbitration record, ensuring that every arbitration sent to the client is valid and well-evidenced
-The working relationship with the client’s Language Manager, including clarifications, escalations, and expectation tracking
Requirements
- Experience: 3 to 5+ years in Localization Quality Assurance (LQA), Senior Language Lead, or Quality Governance roles
- Client and stakeholder management: Direct experience as the primary point of contact for client Language Managers, managing formal arbitration or escalation processes, and facilitating conflict resolution
- Quality audit frameworks: Deep, practical experience with localization evaluation frameworks, including RQE, LQE, error rubrics, and severity mapping
- Style guide and expectation analysis: Ability to analyse style guide changes, identify implicit client expectations, and map tolerance by content type (for example, Marketing vs. Legal vs. UI)
- Meeting facilitation: Hands-on experience with one-to-one coaching, shadowing sessions, alignment roundtables, and structured monthly quality reporting
- Analytical approach: Skill in tracking error concentrations, severity drift, and alignment scores, and in converting justification patterns into style guide improvements
- Language: Native-level Slovak and professional-level English
- Preferred: Prior experience supporting major technology localization programs and working with calibration or alignment tools
Additional Key Information
- Successful candidates will be provided with a dedicated device for project work.
- A background check is required as part of onboarding.
- Candidates must be physically located in one of the approved countries.
Approved countries: Argentina, Australia, Austria, Belgium, Brazil, Bulgaria, Canada, Chile, China, Colombia, Costa Rica, Croatia, Czech Republic, Denmark, Egypt, El Salvador, Finland, France, Germany, Ghana, Greece, Guatemala, Hong Kong, Hungary, India, Indonesia, Ireland, Israel, Italy, Japan, Kenya, Lithuania, Malaysia, Mexico, Netherlands, New Zealand, Nigeria, Norway, Peru, Philippines, Poland, Portugal, Qatar, Romania, Saudi Arabia, Singapore, South Africa, South Korea, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, Taiwan, Thailand, Turkey, United Arab Emirates, United Kingdom, United States and Vietnam.
Why Join Us
This role offers a long-term partnership with global teams on high-visibility products. You will benefit from steady project volume, comprehensive onboarding and ongoing upskilling, and access to established linguistic resources.
If this sounds like the right opportunity, we would love to hear from you.

The role combines creative and editorial expertise with analytical and quality evaluation skills, covering traditional localization work as well as emerging content types, including AI-generated content, linguistic annotation, and structured content evaluations.
With time, the Multimedia Content Reviewer will become the cultural ambassador for their language market and will be expected to produce fully localized content, flag potential cultural issues, and articulate suggestions to make all content appropriate and relevant for the target market.
The ideal candidate possesses a background in journalism, editorial content, copywriting, or a related field, has proven creative writing skills, and a keen attention to detail. Localize, translate, and adapt content of various categories (i.e. multimedia, legal, technical, marketing, sports, entertainment, health and wellness, and other digital content) while adhering to writing style guides and project-specific guidelines.

Write new copy for a range of multimedia products such as music, TV, film, sports, apps, video on-demand, game subscription services, and more.

Copy-edit and fact-check content to ensure accuracy, clarity, consistency, and cultural relevance.

Perform LQA (Localization QA) testing of content published on live platforms (music and app descriptions, marketing material, and marketing campaigns).

Evaluate human-written and AI-generated content for linguistic accuracy, fluency, relevance, consistency, and adherence to project-specific quality standards.

Perform linguistic annotation, content classification, and structured evaluation tasks using predefined guidelines, rating scales, and quality criteria.

Identify and document errors, inconsistencies, and quality issues, providing clear, actionable feedback and supporting rationale for evaluation decisions.

Requirements
BS/BA and 2+ years of work experience in journalism, copywriting, editing, digital media, content production, or a related field.

Experience in translation and localization of multimedia content or demonstrated experience adapting content for Brazilian audiences.

Native-level proficiency in Brazilian Portuguese, with excellent grammar, writing, editing, and linguistic judgment skills.

Ability to quickly detect issues and inconsistencies across large volumes of content and make sound judgment calls based on the information at hand.

Ability to interpret and consistently apply detailed guidelines, rating scales, and evaluation frameworks across different projects.

Familiarity with AI-generated content, linguistic annotation, content evaluation, or data quality assessment is a plus.

Is in tune with and has a wide range of knowledge of music, film, TV, sports, gaming, technology, and Brazilian pop culture.

Has the ability to own linguistic quality for the Brazilian Portuguese market and make confident linguistic decisions.

Must be highly detail-oriented with the ability to multitask, prioritize, and meet deadlines.

Fluency in written and verbal English.

Strong computer literacy; knowledge of iOS/macOS systems is a plus.

Ability to work independently and remotely.

Collaborative; enjoys teamwork in a multicultural environment and is open to feedback, calibration, and continuous learning.

Project Hydrus is a scripted and conversational audio data collection project. The recordings produced help build natural, everyday-sounding synthesized voices for conversational AI products — voices that sound like real people talking, not scripted performances.
As Session Director, you'll lead live recording sessions with Voice Contributors, guiding them through scripted scenarios to produce natural, conversational-quality audio. What You'll Do
- Direct voice performers through scripted scenarios, coaching for natural, conversational delivery rather than verbatim recitation.
- Build quick scene context for performers (who, where, why) and improvise to fill narrative or dialogue gaps live, keeping sessions flowing naturally.
- Adapt scripted wording for natural phrasing and regional/dialect authenticity as needed.
- Monitor and correct technical audio quality in real time: mic technique, pacing, clarity, and background noise.
- Manage session pacing to meet recording targets without sacrificing performance quality, and maintain organized notes on adjustments and retakes.
- Create a supportive, low-pressure environment for performers, including those with limited prior voice experience.
What We're Looking For
Required
- Native fluency in the required language (with specific dialect), with a strong ear for natural, colloquial phrasing.
- Experience directing, coaching, or producing voice or audio talent (e.g., voice direction, casting direction, audio/podcast production, dubbing/ADR, or theater direction).
- Demonstrated ability to give clear, specific, actionable performance direction.
- Strong working knowledge of basic recording/mic technique (proximity, plosives, room noise, levels).
- Comfortable improvising and adjusting scripted material on the spot.
- Excellent interpersonal skills; able to build rapport quickly with performers of varying experience levels.
Preferred (nice to have, not required)
- Background in improv, theater direction, or acting coaching.

- Familiarity with DAWs or recording software (e.g., Pro Tools, Adobe Audition, Reaper) for spot-checking audio quality.

About the Role
We are looking for a detail-oriented QC Reviewer to ensure the quality and consistency of robot manipulation video annotations produced by our annotation team. You'll review labeled video segments against a detailed style guide and reference examples, catch errors or inconsistencies, and provide clear, constructive feedback to annotators. This role is critical to maintaining the accuracy and reliability of training data used for robotics AI models.
What You'll Do
- Review completed annotations of robot manipulation videos across three levels of labeling detail (atomic motion, skill/subtask, task/goal).
- Cross-check annotator descriptions against all three camera views (overhead and both wrist-mounted cameras) to verify accuracy of described actions, object identification, and contact/grasp details.
- Verify full coverage of each video — confirm there are no gaps in labeling, including idle or pause moments.
- Check that descriptions accurately reflect what actually happened in the video, including failures, drops, or slipped grips — flagging any instances where outcomes were inaccurately described or "smoothed over."
- Evaluate annotations for adherence to the style guide: correct vocabulary usage, spatial/directional accuracy, consistent terminology for objects and actions, and appropriate language variation (avoiding repetitive phrasing).
- Identify recurring errors or patterns of confusion among annotators and report them to the team lead for calibration purposes.
- Provide specific, actionable feedback on rejected or revised annotations, referencing the style guide and reference examples.
- Participate in periodic calibration sessions with the team and client to align QC standards with evolving guidelines or edge-case resolutions.
- Maintain a QC log or tracking sheet documenting review outcomes, common error types, and annotator performance trends (as required by the project).

What We're Looking For
Required:
- Excellent written English and strong reading comprehension — you'll be evaluating precise, nuanced language choices, not just checking for typos.
- Exceptional attention to detail — able to catch subtle mismatches between video content and written description (e.g., a mislabeled grasp type, an incorrect object part, a missed failure event).
- Strong grasp of spatial/mechanical description (left/right, above/below, object parts like handles, lids, edges) to verify annotator accuracy.
- Ability to apply a detailed, structured style guide consistently and make sound judgment calls in ambiguous or edge-case scenarios.
- Comfort giving clear, specific, and constructive feedback to annotators (written feedback, not just pass/fail marks).
- Reliable, self-directed work habits, with the ability to work independently while meeting review turnaround expectations.
Nice to Have:
- Prior experience in a QC, editing, proofreading, or annotation review role.
- Experience with video annotation, data labeling, or transcription QA specifically.
- Familiarity with robotics terminology (grippers, end-effectors, manipulation).
- Experience with annotation tools such as Label Studio, including review/approval workflows.

In this role, you will lead a cohort of AI Trainers/Data Annotators within your locale, conduct rigorous quality evaluations, run targeted calibration and upskilling sessions, and extract meaningful data insights for client stakeholders.
You will serve as the bridge between ground-level annotation workflows and strategic quality initiatives, ensuring our Large Language Model (LLM) training outputs meet rigorous linguistic criteria.
Key Responsibilities
1. Quality Assessment & Auditing
Perform continuous spot checks, blind audits, and systematic quality reviews across LLM training workflows (RLHF, SFT, red-teaming, prompt-response evaluation, and data labeling).
Evaluate annotation outputs against client taxonomies, gold standards, and rubric guidelines for factual accuracy, linguistic nuance, tone, safety, and coherence.
Help monitor key performance indicators, like Inter-Annotator Agreement (IAA), error classifications, and First-Time Pass Rates.
2. Trainer Enablement & Coaching
Support in the design and delivery of onboarding, calibration sessions, and targeted refresher workshops to continuously upskill AI trainers.
Provide granular, actionable feedback to individual contributors and facilitate root-cause analyses on recurring annotation errors.
Help maintain and update locale-specific training documentation, guideline appendices, error glossaries, and best-practice cheat sheets.
3. Locale Team Leadership
Serve as the primary point of contact and team lead for trainers within your assigned language/cultural locale (Hindi and Hinglish, specifically)
Address daily workflow escalations, edge cases, and guideline ambiguities directly with the team.
Partner with workforce managers to track trainer throughput, quality trends, and individual development roadmaps.
4. Client Insights & Data Intelligence
Aggregate qualitative and quantitative error data in weekly quality reviews.
Identify systematic data distribution gaps, subtle linguistic drifts, cultural alignment nuances, and model failure modes to present actionable intelligence to the client.
Translate raw quality audits into strategic recommendations for guideline refinements and dataset balancing.
5. Ad Hoc Quality & Operational Support
Assist core Quality Leadership with rapid-turnaround evaluations, and pilot annotation schemas.
Participate in cross-locale calibration rounds to align standards across global working teams.
Perform peer reviews and audits
Support unexpected project ramp-ups, tooling transition tests, and data sanitization tasks as needed.
Required Qualifications
Experience: 7+ years of experience in LLM evaluation/RLHF, content moderation QA, localization QA, translation, MTPE or editorial quality management.
Education: Bachelor’s degree in Linguistics, English, Communications, or a related field
Language & Cultural Expertise: Native or bilingual proficiency in Hindi, accompanied by strong cultural fluency and modern idiom awareness. Professional working proficiency in English.
Preferred Qualifications
Experience gathering, structuring, and visualizing error trends using spreadsheets (Google Sheets/Excel) or BI tools (Tableau, Looker, Metabase).
Demonstrated capability to mentor peers, run calibration workshops, and clearly articulate complex guidelines.
Prior experience working on human-in-the-loop (HITL) pipelines for Tier-1 LLM developers (e.g., prompt engineering, pairwise comparisons, safety red-teaming).
Familiarity with annotation platforms
Working knowledge of basic query languages (SQL) or scripting (Python) for data extraction and reporting.
Experience writing or refining formal annotation guidelines and rubrics.
Key Competencies
Precision & Critical Thinking: Exceptional attention to subtle semantic, factual, and cultural distinctions in text.
Communication: Ability to present technical data findings clearly to both engineering-oriented clients and non-technical annotator cohorts.
Agility: Comfort operating in fast-paced environments where project guidelines and client expectations evolve frequently.
Empathy in Leadership: A constructive coaching style that elevates team performance and morale under strict deadlines.

This role offers a long-term partnership with global teams on high-visibility products. You will benefit from steady project volume, comprehensive onboarding and ongoing upskilling, and access to established linguistic resources.

Adhere to established workflows and processes, including raising queries, reporting issues, and proactively communicating risks or blockers to relevant stakeholders.

Technical Skills
Familiarity with CAT tools (XTM/Phrase), License will be provided.

Utilize Automatic Prompt Generation (APG) tools to create baseline prompts for complex parent-child template clusters.

Run and supervise Automated Prompt Optimization (APO) tool, review the outputs, and flag when the APO reaches deadlocks or plateaus.

Manually draft, test, and refine prompts to navigate complex template architectures, overcome anti-patterns, and handle edge cases where tooling is lacking or broken. Solve edge-case scenarios by designing and refining manual prompts.

Projecten zoals deze zijn over de hele wereld grote doelwitten van fraude. Daarom voert Welo Data gedurende het hele proces fraudecontroles uit om ervoor te zorgen dat het programma wordt nageleefd. Alle accounts die frauduleus worden bevonden, worden onmiddellijk van het project verwijderd.

About the Project
Project Hydrus is a scripted and conversational audio data collection project. The recordings produced help build natural, everyday-sounding synthesized voices for conversational AI products — voices that sound like real people talking, not scripted performances.
As Session Director, you'll lead live recording sessions with Voice Contributors, guiding them through scripted scenarios to produce natural, conversational-quality audio. This hands-on role blends creative direction, coaching, and technical audio judgment — making scripted material sound authentic and unscripted, rather than recited, while keeping sessions moving at a natural pace.
What You'll Do
- Direct voice performers through scripted scenarios, coaching for natural, conversational delivery rather than verbatim recitation.
- Build quick scene context for performers (who, where, why) and improvise to fill narrative or dialogue gaps live, keeping sessions flowing naturally.
- Adapt scripted wording for natural phrasing and regional/dialect authenticity as needed.
- Monitor and correct technical audio quality in real time: mic technique, pacing, clarity, and background noise.
- Manage session pacing to meet recording targets without sacrificing performance quality, and maintain organized notes on adjustments and retakes.
- Create a supportive, low-pressure environment for performers, including those with limited prior voice experience.
What We're Looking For
Required
- Native fluency in the required language (with specific dialect), with a strong ear for natural, colloquial phrasing.
- Experience directing, coaching, or producing voice or audio talent (e.g., voice direction, casting direction, audio/podcast production, dubbing/ADR, or theater direction).
- Demonstrated ability to give clear, specific, actionable performance direction.
- Strong working knowledge of basic recording/mic technique (proximity, plosives, room noise, levels).
- Comfortable improvising and adjusting scripted material on the spot.
- Excellent interpersonal skills; able to build rapport quickly with performers of varying experience levels.
Preferred (nice to have, not required)
- Background in improv, theater direction, or acting coaching.
- Experience directing non-professional or first-time voice talent specifically.
- Familiarity with DAWs or recording software (e.g., Pro Tools, Adobe Audition, Reaper) for spot-checking audio quality.

About the Role
We are looking for detail-oriented annotators to help label robot manipulation videos for AI training purposes. You'll watch short videos of robots performing manipulation tasks (filmed from three synchronized camera angles) and produce precise, structured, natural-language descriptions of the actions taking place. This work directly supports the development of robotics AI models and requires strong written English, sharp observational skills, and the discipline to follow a detailed style guide consistently.
What You'll Do
1. Watch short robot manipulation videos, each filmed from three synchronized camera views (an overhead view and views from each of the robot's two wrist-mounted cameras).
2. Break each video into time segments and write clear, natural-language descriptions for each segment.
3. Apply labels at three levels of detail for each applicable segment:
- Atomic motion (a few seconds) — a single small movement (e.g., "close fingers around the red handle")
- Skill / subtask (several seconds to ~20 seconds) — a complete, meaningful action (e.g., "pick up the red block by its edge")
- Task / goal (up to ~1 minute) — the overall purpose of a sequence of skills (e.g., "place all blocks in the container")

4. Ensure every moment of video is covered by a label at two or more of these levels — no gaps, including idle or pause moments.
5. Accurately describe exactly what happens, including when something doesn't go as planned (a dropped object, a failed grasp, a slipped grip). Precision matters more than making the robot look successful.
6. Cross-reference all three camera angles: use the overhead view to understand the overall scene and object identity, and the close-up wrist views to confirm exact contact and grasp details.
7. Follow a detailed style guide covering vocabulary for actions, spatial relationships, object descriptions, and manner of movement, applying it consistently across many episodes.
8. Participate in periodic calibration sessions to align your labeling with the team and the client's reference examples.

What We're Looking For
Required:
1. Strong written English — you'll write dozens of short, precise descriptive sentences per video and need to vary your language rather than repeating the same phrases.
2. Sharp attention to detail — able to distinguish small differences (a successful grasp vs. a fumble, a push vs. a drag, which specific object part is being touched).
3. Comfort following a detailed, structured style guide and applying it consistently, even in ambiguous or edge-case scenarios.
4. Basic comfort with spatial/mechanical description (left/right, above/below, naming object parts like handles, lids, or edges).
5. Reliable, self-directed work habits — this is often heads-down work with periodic check-ins rather than close supervision.
Nice to Have:
1. Prior experience with video annotation, data labeling, transcription, or QA work.
2. Familiarity with robotics terminology (grippers, end-effectors, manipulation) — helpful but not necessary, as the style guide is self-contained.
3. Experience with annotation tools such as Label Studio.

About Welo Life Sciences

Welo Life Sciences, a Welo Global brand, is a specialized language and technology partner serving pharmaceutical, CRO, and medical device organizations operating in regulated global markets. We deliver regulator-ready translation, linguistic validation, and localization solutions that support clinical trials, pharmacovigilance, regulatory affairs, labeling, and global commercialization. Our approach combines subject matter expertise with ISO-certified quality processes and technology-enabled workflows designed to integrate seamlessly into life sciences operations. With extensive experience supporting global product development and post-market requirements, Welo Life Sciences helps organizations accelerate timelines, protect data integrity, and maintain compliance across languages and regions. All solutions are delivered within a secure, audit-ready framework supported by seven ISO certifications. welolifesciences.com

About the Role
We are looking for experienced English into Lithuanian linguists specializing in Medical Devices and In Vitro Diagnostics (IVD) documentation translation.
Key Responsibilities
Translate medical device and in vitro diagnostics documentation from English (US) into Lithuanian.
Perform Copy Edit (translation review) of translated content, ensuring accuracy, terminology consistency, and compliance with project-specific quality requirements.
Review and address QA feedback and client feedback on flagged linguistic issues.
Meet agreed deadlines and maintain high-quality standards across assigned tasks.
Work within the client's CAT tool environment (memoQ 12.5 or higher), using the provided license.
Follow project-specific instructions and workflows.
Field of Expertise
Medical Devices: Instructions for Use (IFUs), User Manuals, product documentation, labeling, and other medical device-related materials.
In Vitro Diagnostics (IVD): Diagnostic test documentation, instructions for use, product information, labeling, and other IVD-related materials.
Must-Have Criteria
Education and Professional Experience
Applicants must meet at least one of the following criteria:
A degree in Translation, Linguistics, or Language Studies (or an equivalent degree); or
A recognized graduate qualification in another field, plus a minimum of two years of full-time professional translation experience; or
A minimum of five years of full-time professional translation experience.
Relevant Translation Experience
At least two years of professional experience in Life Sciences translation, specifically in Medical Devices and In Vitro Diagnostics (IVD).
Proven experience translating medical documentation in the relevant fields.
Experience limited to patent translation will not be considered sufficient.
Ability to perform both Translation and Copy Edit tasks.
Technical Skills
Mandatory: Experience with memoQ, version 12.5 or higher.
A suitable desktop version of memoQ must be installed. A free version is acceptable; a license will be provided by Welo Global.
Familiarity with Microsoft Word and document editing workflows.
Nice-to-Have
Degree in Medicine, Biology, Biochemistry, Biomedical Sciences, Clinical Research, Translation, Linguistics, Philology, or a related field.
Previous in-house experience within a medical device manufacturer, diagnostics company, or Life Sciences organization.
Experience with ISO standards and quality-controlled translation workflows.
Project Details
Language Pair: English (US) into Lithuanian.
Service Line: Life Sciences – Medical Devices.
Task Types: Translation and Copy Edit.
Expected Capacity: Ongoing weekly availability.
Translation is paid per word, while Copy Edit is compensated per hour or per word, depending on the task size. For smaller Copy Edit assignments, payment will be calculated per word, as minimum fees cannot be offered.
Additional QA feedback checks and client feedback reviews may also be assigned as part of the initial project scope, without a separate purchase order.
Before Applying
Please note that an assessment will be part of our onboarding and quality procedure. Only apply if you are willing to complete the assessment.
Please ensure your latest English CV accurately reflects your Life Sciences and Medical Devices translation experience, including:
Total years of professional translation experience.
Years of experience specifically in Medical Devices and In Vitro Diagnostics.
Examples of medical documentation and content types translated.
Your experience with memoQ (please specify the version used).
Your experience performing both Translation and Copy Edit.
Your contact information (email AND phone number).
Beware of recruitment scams. Welo Global and all of its brands never recruit through direct messages on social media or WhatsApp, and never asks candidates to pay money for a job. Official emails come only from @welocalize.com, @welodata.ai, or @hire.lever.co, and all applications go through jobs.lever.co/weloglobal. Be wary of unexpected offers, generic email addresses (such as Gmail or Yahoo), and requests for fees or sensitive information. Report suspicious messages and learn more: Recognizing Scams and Confirming Legitimate Welocalize Communications – Welo Global
We look forward to receiving your application!
